definition_zh: 已受精的；施过肥的；被加过养分的
definition_en: having already been joined with a male cell, or having already been given nutrients
core_image: 一枚卵细胞表面留下精子进入的小孔，旁边是一块颜色变深的、刚下过肥的土
scene: 蛙卵在池塘里被精子包围后，表面出现一道浅浅的色素分界，标志着它已开始分裂。 Only a fertilized egg will divide, so the pond is thick with cells at different stages.
sceneCN: 这里 fertilized 指「已受精的」（第 1 个义项：卵细胞已完成与精子的融合）；句意为只有已受精的卵才会分裂，因此池塘里满是处于不同阶段的细胞。

pos.zh: 已受精的；（土地）施过肥的；加过养分的

senses.title: Of an egg that has fused with a sperm
senses.definition: having already been joined by a male cell and therefore able to divide
senses.definitionCN: 已被雄性细胞结合，因而能够分裂
senses.example: Only a fertilized egg can begin to cleave.
senses.exampleCN: 只有受精卵才能开始卵裂。
senses.why: the -ed form marks completion: fertilization has already happened, so the cell is no longer waiting.
senses.whyCN: -ed 形式标记完成：受精已经发生，因此这个细胞不再处于等待状态。

senses.title: Of soil that has been fed
senses.definition: having had nutrients added so that it can support stronger growth
senses.definitionCN: 已加入养分，因而能支撑更强的生长
senses.example: The fertilized soil held moisture far better than the bare plot.
senses.exampleCN: 施过肥的土壤比裸露地块的保水能力强得多。
senses.why: the same participle applies because the soil has received exactly what the verb supplies.
senses.whyCN: 同一分词同样适用，因为土壤接收了动词所提供的东西。

senses.title: Of a field or pasture already treated
senses.titleCN: 已施过肥的田地或牧场
senses.definition: having already received fertilizer before planting or grazing
senses.definitionCN: 在播种或放牧之前已经施过肥
senses.example: Cattle were moved onto the fertilized pasture in May.
senses.exampleCN: 五月里牛群被赶进施过肥的牧场。
senses.why: land is treated as a patient that receives an action, so the participle describes its finished state.
senses.whyCN: 土地被当作接受动作的对象，分词因此描述它已完成的状态。

senses.title: Of a lawn or garden already fed
senses.titleCN: 已施过肥的草坪或花园
senses.definition: having been given lawn or garden feed and showing the result
senses.definitionCN: 已施以草坪或园艺肥料，并显出效果
senses.example: The fertilized lawn greened up within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 施过肥的草坪一周内就绿了起来。
senses.why: the visible result is the point: the participle implies not only the act but its effect on appearance.
senses.whyCN: 可见的结果才是重点：这个分词不仅暗示动作，还暗示它对长势的影响。

senses.title: Of water oversupplied with nutrients
senses.definition: having received so many nutrients that algae grow out of control
senses.definitionCN: 接受的养分过多，以致藻类失控生长
senses.example: The fertilized pond was closed to swimming that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那个养分过剩的池塘当年夏天禁止游泳。
senses.why: the same completion marker turns neutral when the amount is excessive: fed becomes overfed.
senses.whyCN: 当数量过度时，同一个完成标记转为负面：被喂养变成了被喂过头。

senses.title: Of a flower that received pollen
senses.definition: having received pollen on its stigma and therefore able to set seed
senses.definitionCN: 柱头已接受花粉，因而能够结实
senses.example: Every fertilized flower in the row set a pod.
senses.exampleCN: 这一行里每一朵受过粉的花都结了荚。
senses.why: in plants the delivery must be complete before fusion, so the participle can mark the earlier stage as finished too.
senses.whyCN: 在植物中投递必须先完成才可能融合，因此这个分词也可标记更早的阶段已结束。

senses.title: Of a pregnancy begun from such a cell
senses.definition: describing a pregnancy that began with a fertilized egg that implanted
senses.definitionCN: 描述由已着床的受精卵开始的妊娠
senses.example: The scan showed a fertilized ovum correctly placed in the uterus.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示受精卵正确地着床在子宫内。
senses.why: the adjective follows the cell into its next role, so the same word describes the start of a pregnancy.
senses.whyCN: 形容词跟着这个细胞进入下一个角色，因此同一个词也描述妊娠的开端。

senses.title: Figurative: a mind made more productive
senses.titleCN: 比喻：被丰富、被激发的（头脑）
senses.definition: figurative, having been supplied with something that makes thought more productive
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，已获得某种使思维更有产出的东西
senses.example: A fertilized imagination invents connections that a dry one misses.
senses.exampleCN: 被丰富的想像力能想出干枯头脑错过的联系。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the completion: the enriching has already taken place and its effect is visible.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了完成义：丰富作用已经发生，其效果可见。

intro.en: Fertilized is the past participle of fertilize, from Medieval Latin fertilizare, built on fertilis 'fruitful' and ultimately ferre 'to bear'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fertilized 是 fertilize 的过去分词，后者来自中世纪拉丁 fertilizare，建立在 fertilis「能结果的」之上，最终出自 ferre「承载」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre 'to bear, carry' supplies the idea of bearing fruit; its pre-Latin origin is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: ferre「承载、生育」提供「结果实」的意思；它在拉丁语之前的来源属重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Fertilis 'fruitful' is generally analysed as ferre plus -ilis 'able'; the intermediate form is unattested.
items.cn: fertilis「能结果的」一般分析为 ferre 加 -ilis「能够」；中间形式没有书证。

items.en: Fertilizare 'to make fruitful' passed from land to living things over several centuries.
items.cn: fertilizare「使之结果」在数百年间从土地扩展到生物。

items.en: English -ed marks a completed action or a resulting state, which is why fertilized can describe an egg, a field or a pond.
items.cn: 英语的 -ed 标记已完成的动作或由此形成的状态，因此 fertilized 可以描述卵、田地或池塘。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first recorded use of the participle for a gamete is not established; the dates and stages above are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个分词首次用于配子的记录尚未确定；以上年代与阶段均为约数。

note.en: Group one separates the -ed forms that look alike; group two separates states of being supplied from states of being joined.
note.cn: 第一组区分外形相近的 -ed 形式；第二组区分「已被供给」与「已被结合」两种状态。

entries.definition: Able to produce; it describes a capacity, while fertilized describes a completed event.
entries.definitionCN: 能够出产；描述能力，而 fertilized 描述已完成的事件。

entries.definition: The material itself, formed with -er; it has no tense and cannot describe a field.
entries.definitionCN: 物质本身，由 -er 构成；它没有时态，不能描述田地。

entries.definition: The active participle: the work is under way, whereas fertilized means the work is finished.
entries.definitionCN: 主动分词：工作正在进行，而 fertilized 表示工作已完成。

entries.definition: From sterile, not fertile, plus -ize: made free of living organisms, almost the reverse of fertilized soil.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 sterile 而非 fertile，加 -ize：使不含活体，几乎与施过肥的土壤相反。

entries.definition: Having been made pregnant, or having been soaked through with a substance; broader than fertilized.
entries.definitionCN: 已被致孕，或已被某种物质浸透；比 fertilized 更宽。

entries.definition: Having received pollen; this marks the delivery, while fertilized marks the fusion.
entries.definitionCN: 已接受花粉；标记投递完成，而 fertilized 标记融合完成。

entries.definition: Having been given more of something valuable; it lacks the specific growth image of fertilized.
entries.definitionCN: 已获得更多有价值之物；缺少 fertilized 那种生长的具体意象。

entries.definition: A neutral participle for having undergone a process; fertilized is narrower because it names which substance was added.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的分词，指经历过某种处理；fertilized 更窄，因为它指明加入了什么。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the -ed ending, the real noun pair and the real opposites.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：-ed 词尾、真实的名词配对与真实的反义词。

normal.en: -ed marks completion: the fertilizing is already done.
normal.cn: -ed 标记完成：施肥或受精已经结束。

normal.en: Four objects share the participle: egg, soil, field, lawn.
normal.cn: 四个对象共用这个分词：卵、土壤、田地、草坪。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: fertilized egg, fertilized soil, newly fertilized.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：受精卵、施过肥的土壤、刚受精的。

normal.en: The opposite is unfertilized, formed with the prefix un-.
normal.cn: 反义词是 unfertilized，由前缀 un- 构成。

normal.en: The family runs fertilize, fertilization, fertilizer, fertile, fertility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fertilize、fertilization、fertilizer、fertile、fertility。

abstract.en: Picture an egg with a tiny door that has just closed behind a visitor.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚卵，门刚在来访者身后合上。

abstract.en: Picture dark, moist soil where bare dust used to be.
abstract.cn: 想象深色湿润的土壤，取代了原先裸露的尘土。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that has been watered and now keeps producing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被浇过水的头脑，从此不断产出。

examples.en: The fertilized egg divided for the first time six hours later.
examples.cn: 六小时后，受精卵第一次分裂。

examples.en: The fertilized beds produced twice the usual harvest.
examples.cn: 施过肥的苗圃产量是平常的两倍。

examples.en: Runoff left the pond fertilized and choked with algae.
examples.cn: 径流使池塘养分过剩，藻类疯长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fertilize + ed」——受精或施肥这个动作已经做完 → 已受精的、施过肥的

root: 拉丁 fertilis「能结果的」= ferre「承载、生育」+ -ilis「能够」；fertilizare「使结果」；英语 fertilize + -ed。ferre 的印欧来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of fertilized share one grammatical fact: the supplying or joining is already complete, so what is described is a finished state.
sensesIntro.cn: fertilized 的八个义项共有一个语法事实：供给或结合已经完成，因此被描述的是一个完成后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finished act leaves its mark on the thing that received it.
core.cn: 核心意象：完成的动作在接受者身上留下痕迹。

branches.en: THE CELL LINE: fusion is complete, and the same cell later begins a pregnancy.
branches.cn: 细胞线：融合已完成，同一个细胞后来开启一段妊娠。

branches.en: THE LAND LINE: soil, pasture and lawn all carry the mark of having been fed.
branches.cn: 土地线：土壤、牧场与草坪都带着「被喂过」的印记。

branches.en: TOO MUCH: the same completion becomes damage when nutrients pile up.
branches.cn: 过量：养分堆积时，同样的完成变成损害。

branches.en: THE FLOWER LINE: pollen delivery can also be marked as done.
branches.cn: 花线：花粉投递同样可以被标记为完成。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: enrichment leaves a visible change in thought.
branches.cn: 头脑线：丰富作用在思维中留下可见的改变。

intro.en: Fertilized is a derived participle, so its suffixes mark both the action and its completion.
intro.cn: fertilized 是派生分词，后缀既标记动作，也标记完成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base ferre 'to bear' reaches English through fertilis and fertilizare; the English -ed adds the perfect aspect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 ferre「承载」经 fertilis 与 fertilizare 进入英语；英语的 -ed 加上完成体。

items.example: The root carries the image of bearing fruit.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「结果实」的意象。

items.example: Fertilis means able to bear.
Fertilize means to make fruitful.

items.meaningCN: 已完成的动作或由此形成的状态
items.example: Fertilized means the work is done.
items.exampleCN: fertilized 意为这件事已经做完。

items.example: An unfertilized egg never divides.

items.meaning: to make fruitful, to join gametes
items.example: Bees fertilize the blossoms.

items.meaning: the act or result of fertilizing
items.example: Fertilization was observed under the lens.
The fertilizer was worked into the topsoil.
Fertility depends on soil structure.

definition_zh: 全神贯注地；入迷地；着了魔似地
definition_en: in a state of complete attention, as if carried away
core_image: 一圈人围坐着听故事，谁也没有动一下
scene: 孩子们围在火边听故事，连呼吸都放轻了。 The children listened raptly by the fire and hardly dared to breathe.
sceneCN: 这里 raptly 指全神贯注地（第 1 个义项：听得入迷）；句意为孩子们围在火边听故事，连呼吸都放轻了。

senses.title: Absorbed in something
senses.definition: with attention so complete that the self and the surroundings drop away
senses.definitionCN: 专注到忘我、周围的一切都退开
senses.example: The hall listened raptly as the old man told his story.
senses.exampleCN: 老人讲故事时，整个大厅的人都听得入迷。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense: raptly describes attention that has been taken over, not attention merely offered.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常最常用的一层：raptly 写的是注意力被拿走，而不是自己把注意力交出去。

senses.title: In a state of rapture
senses.titleCN: 欣喜若狂地；如痴如醉地
senses.definition: carried out of oneself by joy or wonder
senses.definitionCN: 因喜悦或惊叹而忘形
senses.example: She smiled raptly at the first snow of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 看着那年第一场雪，她欣喜若狂地笑了。
senses.why: The older sense survives in rapture: the feeling is joy, not study.
senses.whyCN: 更古老的一层保存在 rapture（狂喜）里：这里是被喜悦带走，不是读书读到入迷。

intro.en: Raptly is the adverb of rapt, from Latin raptus, 'seized and carried away'.
intro.cn: raptly 是 rapt 的副词，rapt 来自拉丁语 raptus（被抓住并带走）。

items.en: Rapere meant to seize and carry off.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住并带走。

items.en: Raptus named the act of being carried away.
items.cn: raptus 指被带走的状态。

items.en: English used rapt for a mind lifted out of itself.
items.cn: 英语用 rapt 指脱离自身的头脑。

items.en: The same root gave rapture, a transport of joy.
items.cn: 同一词根给出 rapture（狂喜的忘形）。

items.en: Today rapt usually means absorbed, not ecstatic.
items.cn: 今天 rapt 通常指专注，而不是狂喜。

note.en: The look-alike group is the rapt- family; the near-meaning group separates attentively, intently, engrossed and spellbound.
note.cn: 形近组是 rapt 词族；近义组把「专注地」「专心地」「全神投入」「着迷」分开。

entries.definition: deeply absorbed.
entries.definitionCN: 深深投入的。

entries.definition: very fast.
entries.definitionCN: 非常快的。

entries.definition: a feeling of intense delight.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的喜悦。

entries.definition: to cover something.
entries.definitionCN: 包起来。

entries.definition: with careful attention.
entries.definitionCN: 带着细致的注意力。

entries.definition: with strong fixed purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 带着强烈而固定的目的。

entries.definition: fully occupied by something.
entries.definitionCN: 被某事完全占据的。

entries.definition: held as if by magic.
entries.definitionCN: 像被魔法定住的。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a circle of listeners who have stopped moving.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「一圈听者连动都不动了」的画面。

normal.en: Raptly comes from rapt, which means carried off: attention kidnaps you.
normal.cn: raptly 来自 rapt（被带走）：注意力把你绑走了。

normal.en: Picture a fire, a story and a row of still faces.
normal.cn: 想象一堆火、一个故事，和一排静止的脸。

normal.en: Say RAPT-lee; it sounds like wrapped, as if wrapped up in a story.
normal.cn: 读 RAPT-lee，听起来像 wrapped，仿佛被故事裹住。

normal.en: The word describes the outside as much as the inside: nobody moves.
normal.cn: 这个词既写内心也写外表：没有人动。

normal.en: Ask whether the attention was given or taken.
normal.cn: 问一句：这份注意力是被付出的，还是被夺走的？

abstract.en: Raptly is what attention looks like when it stops being effort.
abstract.cn: raptly 是注意力不再费力时的样子。

abstract.en: The word remembers its violent root: to be absorbed is to be carried away.
abstract.cn: 这个词记得它暴烈的词根：被吸住就是被带走。

abstract.en: A rapt audience is a gift and a risk, because it can be held by anything.
abstract.cn: 入迷的观众是礼物也是风险，因为它可以被任何东西握住。

examples.en: The crowd watched raptly as the rope walker crossed the gap.
examples.cn: 走绳者越过缺口时，人群全神贯注地看着。

examples.en: She read raptly until the lamp burned out.
examples.cn: 她读得入迷，直到灯油耗尽。

examples.en: The students were raptly absorbed in the experiment.
examples.cn: 学生们完全被实验吸住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: rapt（被带走）+ ly → 魂被带走般地听着。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住带走）→ raptus

sensesIntro.en: Raptly has two senses: attention taken over by something outside you, and the rarer rapture that the noun rapture still keeps.
sensesIntro.cn: raptly 有两层：被身外之物接管的注意力，以及名词 rapture 仍然保留的那层较罕见的狂喜。

core.en: A STILL RING OF LISTENERS
core.cn: 一圈静止的听者

branches.en: An ear, an eye or a page that takes the mind.
branches.cn: 把心神拿走的耳朵、眼睛或书页。

branches.en: A body that stops moving while a story lasts.
branches.cn: 故事还在，身体已经不动。

branches.en: Joy that lifts a person out of himself.
branches.cn: 把人带出自身的喜悦。

branches.en: Both are states of being carried away.
branches.cn: 两者都是被带走的状态。

branches.en: The warmer, older sense kept in rapture.
branches.cn: 保存在 rapture 里更温暖、更古老的一层。

intro.en: The rapt- family keeps the sense of being carried off: rapt, raptly, rapture and enraptured all describe a mind taken somewhere else.
intro.cn: rapt 词族保留「被带走」的意思：rapt、raptly、rapture、enraptured 都描述被带到别处的头脑。

latinIntro.en: Latin rapere gives raptus, the participle of seizure; English kept the image and softened the violence into delight or attention.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rapere 给出分词 raptus（被夺取）；英语保留意象，把暴力软化成喜悦或专注。

items.example: Listen raptly.
A rapt expression.
A moment of rapture.
A curious raptness.
An enraptured audience.
The music enraptured them.
A word of seizure.
A rapid response.

definition_zh: adj. 荒凉的，光秃秃的；阴冷的；无望的
definition_en: bare and exposed to wind; cold and raw; offering little hope for the future
core_image: 一面没有树的斜坡，枯草贴地，风从坡上直直刮下来
scene: 山坡上没有一棵树，风把枯草吹得沙沙作响。 The hillside was bleak, with no trees at all and wind rattling the dry grass.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bleak 指荒凉无遮蔽；句意是那片山坡没有一棵树，只有风吹枯草。

senses.title: Bare and exposed to weather
senses.definition: empty of trees or shelter and open to wind and cold
senses.definitionCN: 没有树木或遮蔽，暴露在风寒之中
senses.example: The cottage stood on a bleak moor with nothing behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 小屋立在一片荒原上，身后一无所有。
senses.why: The old word meant pale, and pale land is land with no green cover.
senses.whyCN: 这个古词本义是「苍白」，而苍白的土地就是没有绿意覆盖的土地。

senses.title: Cold and raw
senses.definition: of weather or wind, unpleasantly cold and damp
senses.definitionCN: 天气或风阴冷潮湿，令人不适
senses.example: A bleak wind came off the water all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都有一股阴冷的风从水面吹来。
senses.why: Colour drains from a scene as cold drains warmth from it, so the same word names both.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷抽走暖意，就像苍白抽走颜色，于是同一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: Offering little hope
senses.definition: of a situation, seeming to offer no comfort or good outcome
senses.definitionCN: 局势显得毫无安慰与转机
senses.example: The report paints a bleak picture for small farms.
senses.exampleCN: 报告为小农场描绘了一幅黯淡的图景。
senses.why: A landscape with no shelter becomes a future with no shelter: the metaphor is spatial before it is emotional.
senses.whyCN: 没有遮蔽的风景变成没有遮蔽的未来：这个比喻先属于空间，后才属于情绪。

intro.en: Bleak came from Old Norse bleikr, pale, and shares its root with bleach.
intro.cn: bleak 来自古诺尔斯语 bleikr（苍白的），与 bleach 同根。

items.en: Bleikr means pale, the colour of land without green.
items.cn: bleikr 意为苍白，即没有绿意的土地之色。

items.en: The English cousin blāc carries the same pale sense.
items.cn: 英语同源词 blāc 同样表示苍白。

items.en: English bleak first describes pale or pallid things.
items.cn: 英语 bleak 最初形容苍白之物。

items.en: The word is applied to bare, windswept country.
items.cn: 该词被用于光秃、多风的地方。

items.en: Writers extend it to cold weather and grim situations.
items.cn: 作家把它扩展到寒冷天气与严峻处境。

items.en: Bleak now most often means without hope.
items.cn: 现代 bleak 最常表示没有希望。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the bl- start and the pale root; the near-meaning group runs from empty land to a hopeless forecast.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bl- 开头与「苍白」词根；近义组从空荡的土地排到无望的预期。

entries.definition: To make something white.
entries.definitionCN: 使变白。

entries.definition: The cry of a sheep.
entries.definitionCN: 羊的叫声。

entries.definition: Dim and watery, as tired eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 模糊朦胧，如疲惫的眼睛。

entries.definition: To draw back in fear.
entries.definitionCN: 因恐惧而退缩。

entries.definition: Empty, bare and without comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 空旷荒凉、毫无慰藉。

entries.definition: Too poor to grow plants.
entries.definitionCN: 贫瘠得长不出植物。

entries.definition: Serious and without cheer.
entries.definitionCN: 严肃而毫无欢意。

entries.definition: Dull and depressing.
entries.definitionCN: 沉闷压抑的。

normalIntro.en: A pale hillside with no trees, a cold wind, and a forecast with nothing good in it: all three are bleak.
normalIntro.cn: 没有树的光山坡、一阵冷风、一份没有好消息的预报：三者都叫 bleak。

normal.en: Bleak and bleach share the old word for pale.
normal.cn: bleak 与 bleach 共享表示「苍白」的古词。

normal.en: A pale landscape has no green left on it.
normal.cn: 苍白的风景上没有留下一丝绿。

normal.en: No trees means no shelter, and wind finds you.
normal.cn: 没有树就没有遮蔽，风就能找到你。

normal.en: Cold weather and grim news feel like the same landscape.
normal.cn: 阴冷的天气与黯淡的消息像同一片风景。

normal.en: If a report makes you shiver, it is bleak.
normal.cn: 如果一份报告让你发冷，它就是 bleak。

abstract.en: A hillside with nothing standing on it.
abstract.cn: 一寸立着的东西也没有的山坡。

abstract.en: Warmth and colour both withdrawn.
abstract.cn: 暖意与颜色同时被抽走。

abstract.en: A horizon that offers no next step.
abstract.cn: 不提供下一步的地平线。

examples.en: The mining town looks bleak in February.
examples.cn: 这座矿镇在二月显得一片荒凉。

examples.en: Analysts gave a bleak assessment of the currency.
examples.cn: 分析师对本国货币作出了黯淡的评估。

examples.en: They walked all day across bleak, treeless country.
examples.cn: 他们整天穿行在荒凉无树的地带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不留客」——荒凉到这种地步，谁都留不住，风也得赶快走。

root: 古诺尔斯语 bleikr（苍白的）；与古英语 blāc、现代英语 bleach 同源

sensesIntro.en: The senses all describe withdrawal: green withdrawn, warmth withdrawn, hope withdrawn.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在描述「被抽走」：抽走绿色、抽走暖意、抽走希望。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a treeless slope under grey wind, grass pressed flat
core.cn: 核心意象：灰风下的无树山坡，草被压平

branches.en: A moor with one broken wall.
branches.cn: 只有一道断墙的荒原。

branches.en: A field with no hedge left.
branches.cn: 篱笆全无的田野。

branches.en: Wind coming straight off the sea.
branches.cn: 直从海上刮来的风。

branches.en: A forecast with no good line in it.
branches.cn: 找不到好消息的预报。

branches.en: A view that offers nothing to stand behind.
branches.cn: 不提供任何可依靠之物的景象。

intro.en: Bleak is an adjective with regular English endings; the list below builds its forms and the vocabulary of bare, cold scenes.
intro.cn: bleak 是带规则英语词尾的形容词；下面列出它的各种形式，以及荒凉阴冷词场的词缀。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pallere 意为发白，vastare 意为使荒芜，frigere 意为寒冷。

definition_zh: 习惯性地；一贯地；经常地
definition_en: in a way that is done regularly because it has become a habit
core_image: 散会时同一个人总把椅子推回桌下，即便当天他不是最后走的人
scene: 每次散会前，同一个人总会把椅子推回桌下，即使那天他不是最后离开的人。 He habitually checks the locks twice before leaving, even in daylight.
sceneCN: 这里本词指出于长期习惯而反复做（第 1 个义项：以习惯性的方式）；句意为他在离开前习惯性地检查两遍门锁，即使是在白天。

derivatives.zh: 去掉表方式的副词后缀后得到形容词，语义为「惯常的、已成习惯的」
由形容词去掉形容词后缀后得到名词，语义为「习惯、习性」
由名词加表「使成为」的动词后缀构成，语义偏移为「使习惯」
由动词加表动作或结果的后缀构成，语义偏移为「习惯化」
由形容词加表性质的名词后缀构成，语义偏移为「惯常性」

senses.title: By force of habit
senses.definition: in a way produced by a repeated pattern rather than a fresh decision
senses.definitionCN: 由反复形成的模式促成，而非每次重新决定
senses.example: He habitually checks the locks twice before leaving, even in daylight.
senses.exampleCN: 他在离开前习惯性地检查两遍门锁，即使是在白天。
senses.why: The adverb is the habit adjective plus a manner suffix, so it says that a habit is the reason for the doing.
senses.whyCN: 该副词由「习惯」形容词加表方式的后缀构成，因此说明做事的缘由是习惯。

senses.title: As a settled rule
senses.definition: as a regular rule of behaviour, with few exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 作为几乎无例外的一贯做法
senses.example: She is habitually the first to arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 她一向是第一个到的人。
senses.why: A rule kept across many occasions is the adverb's sense of consistency.
senses.whyCN: 在许多场合都保持的规则，就是该副词「一贯」的意思。

senses.title: Frequently, over and over
senses.definition: often and repeatedly, as a matter of course
senses.definitionCN: 经常而反复，且被视为常态
senses.example: Trucks habitually exceed the weight limit on this bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车经常超载通过这座桥。
senses.why: Frequency grows out of repetition, so the adverb also means often.
senses.whyCN: 频率由反复而来，因此该副词也指「经常」。

senses.title: Without thinking about it
senses.definition: with no deliberate attention at the moment of doing
senses.definitionCN: 在做的一刻并没有刻意留意
senses.example: He habitually reaches for the second cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他下意识地又伸手去拿第二个杯子。
senses.why: A habit runs itself, so the adverb can mark an act done without a fresh thought.
senses.whyCN: 习惯自行运转，因此该副词可标出未加新思考的动作。

senses.title: According to institutional practice
senses.definition: following the accepted course of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 按照机构认可的程序
senses.example: The clerk habitually files the forms before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员照例在中午前归档表格。
senses.why: A group's repeated practice turns into a course of action the adverb can describe.
senses.whyCN: 群体反复的做法会变成一条可被该副词描述的行动路线。

senses.title: From dependence
senses.definition: in a way driven by a compulsion rather than a choice
senses.definitionCN: 由强迫性依赖而非选择驱动
senses.example: The patient habitually used the painkiller for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这名患者多年来习惯性使用这种止痛药。
senses.why: Compulsion is habit with the grip tightened, and the adverb follows it.
senses.whyCN: 成瘾是「抓得更紧」的习惯，该副词也随之延伸。

senses.title: As a described pattern in law or reports
senses.titleCN: 惯常地（法律与报告用语）
senses.definition: in formal description, in a way that repeats as a pattern
senses.definitionCN: 在正式描述中，以反复成模式的方式
senses.example: The report notes that the firm habitually underreports emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出该企业惯常少报排放量。
senses.why: Formal writing uses the adverb to state a pattern without judging each instance.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作使用该副词陈述模式，而不逐次评判。

senses.title: As part of a daily rhythm
senses.definition: at the same points in a daily or seasonal cycle
senses.definitionCN: 在每日或季节循环的同一时点
senses.example: The herd habitually moves to the river at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 兽群照例在黄昏走向河边。
senses.why: A rhythm kept by repetition is another face of habit, applied to daily timing.
senses.whyCN: 由重复维持的节律是习惯的另一面，用于日常时间安排。

intro.en: Habitually is habitual plus the native manner suffix -ly; habitual comes from Latin habitualis, from habitus 'condition', from habere 'to hold'.
intro.cn: 本词由 habitual 加英语本族方式后缀构成；habitual 来自拉丁语 habitualis，出自 habitus「状态」，词根为 habere「持有」。

items.en: Habere 'to have, hold' supplied the root for words about a held condition.
items.cn: habere「拥有、持有」为表「被持有的状态」的词提供词根。

items.en: Habitus named a settled condition or bearing, and gave English the noun habit.
items.cn: habitus 指稳定的状态或举止，并给英语提供了名词「习惯」。

items.en: Habitualis added an adjective suffix meaning 'of the kind of', describing what belongs to such a condition.
items.cn: 加上表「属于该类」的形容词后缀后，描述属于这种状态的东西。

items.en: English formed the adjective from the noun and then added the native manner suffix, recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语由名词构成形容词，再加本族方式后缀构成副词，最早见于十六世纪。

items.en: Reports, law and zoology later used the adverb for patterns that repeat without a person deciding each time.
items.cn: 报告、法律与动物学后来用该副词指不必每次由人决定的反复模式。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the Indo-European base behind habere is generally considered to be a reconstruction; the first adverb citation is not exact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：habere 背后的印欧词基一般认为是重构形式；该副词最早书证年代并不精确。

note.en: Group one holds close forms from the same holding root; group two holds adverbs for what happens again and again.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「持有」词根的形近形式；第二组是表示反复发生的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a repeated pattern; it modifies a noun rather than a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 描述反复模式的形容词，修饰名词而非动词。

entries.definition: The noun naming the pattern itself, with neither adjective nor adverb ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指模式本身的名词，不带形容词或副词后缀。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to accustom, formed with a suffix meaning 'make'.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「使习惯」的动词，由表「使成为」的后缀构成。

entries.definition: From the same root through a dwelling verb; it names where something lives.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词经表居住的动词而来，指某物生活之处。

entries.definition: In most cases, said of frequency without the idea of a formed habit.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，只说频率，不含「已成习惯」的意思。

entries.definition: As part of a set procedure, stressing the schedule rather than the person's grip.
entries.definitionCN: 作为固定程序的一部分，强调流程而非个人的黏着。

entries.definition: At steady intervals, with attention to timing rather than to compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 按稳定间隔发生，关注时间而非强迫性。

entries.definition: As a usual feature of a person or group, said of what is representative.
entries.definitionCN: 作为人或群体的通常特征，指代表性表现。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adverb is the habit adjective plus the native manner suffix.
normal.cn: 该副词由「习惯」形容词加英语本族方式后缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs habit, habitual, habitually, habituate, habituation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括习惯、惯常的、习惯性地、使习惯、习惯化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: habitually late, habitually absent, habitually silent.
normal.cn: 固定说法：惯常迟到、经常缺席、一贯沉默。

normal.en: The adverb can describe a person, a group, an animal herd or a formal report.
normal.cn: 该副词可描述个人、群体、兽群或正式报告。

normal.en: Its force is weaker than deliberately and stronger than occasionally.
normal.cn: 它的力度弱于「故意地」，强于「偶尔」。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pushed under the table before anyone asks.
abstract.cn: 想象还没人开口，椅子已被推回桌下。

abstract.en: Picture a hand checking a pocket that has been empty all day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去摸一个空了一整天的口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a herd turning toward the river before the sun has moved.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳还没移动，兽群已转向河边。

examples.en: He is habitually late for the morning briefing.
examples.cn: 他早上的例会惯常迟到。

examples.en: The staff habitually wipe the benches before opening.
examples.cn: 员工习惯性地在开门前擦净长椅。

examples.en: Such firms habitually underreport their waste.
examples.cn: 这类企业惯常少报废弃量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「惯常的」加表方式的副词后缀——以属于习惯的方式去做，就是习惯性地、经常地。

root: 英语 habitual 加本族方式副词后缀；habitual 出自拉丁 habitualis，词根为 habere「拥有、持有」，由「被保持的状态」引申为反复成习；更深词基一般认为是重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one manner: a habit explains the act, then the act becomes a rule, a frequency, a reflex, a procedure, a dependency, a reported pattern and a daily rhythm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种方式展开：习惯解释行为，行为再成为规则、频率、反射、程序、依赖、报告中的模式与日常节律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chair pushed back under the table before anyone has asked.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人开口，椅子已被推回桌下。

branches.en: HABIT AS REASON: the plain sense gives habit as the cause, and a cause kept across occasions becomes a rule.
branches.cn: 习惯为因：最普通的义项把习惯当原因，而在多个场合保持的原因就成了规则。

branches.en: REPETITION IN TIME: frequency and daily rhythm are the same repetition seen as count and as clock.
branches.cn: 时间中的反复：频率与日常节律是同一反复在「次数」与「时钟」两个角度上的样子。

branches.en: WITHOUT A FRESH THOUGHT: the doing runs itself, with no decision taken at the moment, which is how habit becomes reflex.
branches.cn: 无需新念头：行为自行运转，当下并不作决定，习惯由此成为反射。

branches.en: INSTITUTION AND DEPENDENCE: a procedure is a group's habit, a dependency is habit with the grip tightened.
branches.cn: 机构与依赖：程序是群体的习惯，依赖是抓得更紧的习惯。

branches.en: REPORTED PATTERN: formal writing names a pattern without judging each case.
branches.cn: 被报告的模式：正式写作陈述模式，而不逐案评判。

intro.en: Habitually is an adjective plus a native manner suffix; the adjective is a Latin noun of condition plus an adjective suffix, so the word reads in three parts.
intro.cn: 本词是形容词加英语本族方式后缀；形容词本身是拉丁状态名词加形容词后缀，因此可分三部分读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere supplies the root through habitus, and the adjective suffix marks belonging to a kind; the manner suffix is native English with no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「持有」的动词经其状态名词提供词根，形容词后缀表「属于某类」；方式后缀是英语本族成分，没有拉丁来源。

items.example: The root carries the idea of something held.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「被持有」的意思。

items.example: The noun named a settled condition.
items.exampleCN: 这一名词指稳定的状态。

items.example: Reading became a habit.
The habitual riser beat the alarm.
items.exampleCN: 惯于早起的人比闹钟起得早。

items.example: He habitually checks the locks.
Keepers habituate animals to noise.
items.exampleCN: 饲养员让动物习惯噪声。

items.example: Habituation took four weeks.
The habitualness of the gesture went unnoticed.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作的惯常性无人注意。

items.example: The syrup is habit-forming.
items.exampleCN: 这种糖浆容易使人成瘾。

definition_zh: 君主的；君主制的；拥护君主制的；君主般专断的；以一人为顶点的
definition_en: relating to a monarch or to monarchy; favouring royal rule; or resembling a monarch in manner and structure
core_image: 一份组织图的最上方只画着一个王冠，下面的线全部汇到这一点
scene: 会议室的白板上画着一张架构图，最上方只有一个圆圈，底下所有箭头都汇向它。 The board's monarchic structure gave one chair the final word on every budget.
sceneCN: 这里 monarchic 指「以一人为顶点、像君主制那样组织的」（第 5 个义项：单一首脑结构）；句意为董事会的君主式结构让一把椅子对每项预算拥有最终决定权。可辨识物件：白板、架构图、圆圈、箭头、椅子。

pos.zh: 君主的；君主制的；拥护君主制的；专断的

derivatives.zh: monarchic + -ally（副词后缀）→ 以君主方式地
monarchic 的 -ical 变体，语义相同而语体更正式
monarch + -ism（主义后缀）→ 君主主义，由形容词转为政治主张
monarch + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 君主主义者
monarch + -y（状态后缀）→ 君主制，由属性转回制度
希腊 monarkhes 经拉丁 → 君主，为整个词族的人称基础

senses.title: Relating to a monarch
senses.definition: belonging to the person of a king, queen or emperor
senses.definitionCN: 属于国王、女王或皇帝本人的
senses.example: The monarchic title passed to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 君主称号传给了长子。
senses.why: The suffix -ic makes a relational adjective, so the word simply means 'of a monarch' at its base.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此这个词最基本的意思就是「君主的」。

senses.title: Relating to monarchy as a system
senses.titleCN: 与君主制这一制度相关的
senses.definition: describing the institutions and practices of rule by a hereditary head of state
senses.definitionCN: 描述由世袭元首统治的制度与实践
senses.example: Monarchic government survived in a few small states.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制政府在少数小国中留存下来。
senses.why: Because the adjective can modify 'government' or 'system', it extends from the person to the whole arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个形容词可修饰「政府」或「体系」，便从人扩展到整套安排。

senses.title: Favouring royal rule
senses.definition: supporting the restoration or preservation of a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 支持恢复或保留君主制
senses.example: The monarchic party opposed the referendum.
senses.exampleCN: 拥护君主制的政党反对这次公投。
senses.why: A political adjective often names a stance rather than a fact, so monarchic can mean 'on the side of the crown'.
senses.whyCN: 政治形容词常命名立场而非事实，因此 monarchic 可指「站在王冠一边」。

senses.title: Characteristic of a monarch's manner
senses.definition: showing the assurance, distance or dignity associated with a ruler
senses.definitionCN: 表现出与统治者相关的笃定、距离感或威仪
senses.example: He spoke with a monarchic assurance that ended debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着君主般的笃定说话，终止了辩论。
senses.why: The adjective moves from office to temperament, so an unelected chair can sound monarchic.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从职位移到性情，因此一位非经选举的主席也能显得像君主。

senses.title: Structured with one person at the top
senses.definition: organised so that a single person holds final authority over everyone else
senses.definitionCN: 组织方式使一人对其余所有人握有最终权威
senses.example: The board's monarchic structure gave one chair the final word on every budget.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会的君主式结构让一把椅子对每项预算拥有最终决定权。
senses.why: The political shape is applied to an organisation, where one signature can override a whole committee.
senses.whyCN: 政治形态被套用到组织上，一个签名便可压倒整个委员会。

senses.title: Of a state with a crowned head
senses.definition: describing a country whose head of state holds a royal title
senses.definitionCN: 描述元首拥有王室称号的国家
senses.example: Monarchic states dominated the peninsula for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制国家曾支配这个半岛数百年。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the state as well as to the office, since a country can be described by its constitutional form.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也修饰国家，因为一国可由其宪制形式来描述。

senses.title: Domineering in personal habit
senses.definition: acting as though one's word cannot be questioned, like an absolute ruler
senses.definitionCN: 行事仿佛自己的话不容置疑，像绝对统治者
senses.example: Her monarchic habits alienated the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她专断的作风让员工疏远了她。
senses.why: The critical use turns the adjective from description into reproach: a small tyrant in an office.
senses.whyCN: 批评性用法把这个形容词从描述变为责备：办公室里的一个小暴君。

senses.title: Of a particular royal era
senses.definition: describing a historical period governed by a monarch or a royal regime
senses.definitionCN: 描述由君主或王室政权统治的历史时期
senses.example: Monarchic France collapsed in the revolution.
senses.exampleCN: 君主制的法国在大革命中崩溃。
senses.why: Historians use the adjective to label a regime and its era, just as they use dynastic for a ruling house.
senses.whyCN: 史家用这个形容词标记政权及其时代，正如用 dynastic 标记统治家族。

intro.en: Monarchic is the Greek adjective monarkhikos, built on monarkhes 'sole ruler' with the suffix -ikos, which Latin reshaped as -icus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monarchic 是希腊形容词 monarkhikos，由 monarkhes「唯一统治者」加后缀 -ikos 构成，拉丁语把它改造为 -icus。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos 'alone' supplies the first element of the compound, as in monologue and monopoly.
items.cn: monos「单独」提供复合词的第一个成分，与 monologue、monopoly 相同。

items.en: Arkhein 'to rule' supplies the second element, shared with hierarchy though the prefixes differ.
items.cn: arkhein「统治」提供第二个成分，与 hierarchy 共享，但前缀不同。

items.en: The adjective monarkhikos meant 'of a sole ruler' or 'fit for a ruler'.
items.cn: 形容词 monarkhikos 意为「唯一统治者的」或「适合统治者的」。

items.en: Latin reshaped Greek -ikos as -icus, the standard relational suffix that English later reduced to -ic.
items.cn: 拉丁把希腊 -ikos 改造为 -icus，这是标准的关系后缀，英语后来简化为 -ic。

items.en: English adopted the adjective beside monarchy and monarch, and later extended it to organisations and personal manner.
items.cn: 英语在 monarchy 与 monarch 旁采纳了这个形容词，后来又扩展到组织与个人作风。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation is not recorded precisely, and the organisational sense has no single documented origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语书证并不确切，组织义也没有唯一可考来源。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same compound or a shared element; group two holds adjectives describing rule by one person.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该复合词或共享成分的形式；第二组是描述一人统治的形容词。

entries.definition: The -ical variant of the same adjective, now the more usual form in political prose.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的 -ical 变体，如今在政治文章中更常用。

entries.definition: The ruler; monarchic is the adjective derived from this person.
entries.definitionCN: 统治者；monarchic 是由这个人称派生的形容词。

entries.definition: The system or state of rule by one; the adjective can modify either this system or its ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 一人统治的制度或国家；该形容词既可修饰制度也可修饰君主。

entries.definition: From monazein 'live alone', with no arkhein element: a monastic house, not a political form.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 monazein「独居」，无 arkhein 成分：是僧院，不是政治形式。

entries.definition: Belonging to a king or queen; it names the rank, while monarchic names the constitutional type.
entries.definitionCN: 属于国王或女王；指等级，而 monarchic 指宪制类型。

entries.definition: Ruling without constitutional checks; it stresses unlimited power rather than inheritance.
entries.definitionCN: 不受宪法制约地统治；强调无限权力而非世袭。

entries.definition: Ruling with arbitrary cruelty; a strongly negative word that monarchic does not always carry.
entries.definitionCN: 专横残暴地统治；贬义很强，而 monarchic 未必带有这层。

entries.definition: Arranged in ranks; it shares the arkhein element but describes any ladder, not one crown.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排列；共享 arkhein 成分，但描述任何阶梯，而非一顶王冠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monarch + -ic: the adjective of one-person rule.
normal.cn: monarch + -ic：一人统治的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs monarchic, monarchical, monarchically, monarch, monarchy, monarchist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monarchic、monarchical、monarchically、monarch、monarchy、monarchist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: monarchic system, monarchic party, monarchic structure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：君主制体系、拥护君主制的政党、单一首脑结构。

normal.en: hierarchy shares arkhein but adds hieros 'sacred', so it is a cousin, not a twin.
normal.cn: hierarchy 共享 arkhein，却加了 hieros「神圣」，因此是表亲而非孪生。

normal.en: The adjective easily slips from describing a state to criticising a boss.
normal.cn: 这个形容词很容易从描述国家滑向批评上司。

abstract.en: Picture an org chart with a crown at the top and no second box.
abstract.cn: 想象一张架构图，顶端是王冠，下面没有第二个框。

abstract.en: Picture a committee where only one pen can sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会，只有一支笔能签字。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where everyone waits for one person to nod.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，所有人都等一个人点头。

examples.en: The monarchic regime lasted until the constitution was rewritten.
examples.cn: 这个君主制政权一直延续到宪法被重写。

examples.en: His monarchic gestures made the committee feel like a court.
examples.cn: 他君主般的姿态让委员会像一座宫廷。

examples.en: The report criticised the monarchic concentration of power in one office.
examples.cn: 报告批评权力君主式地集中在一个办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monarch」君主 + 「ic」的——君主式的、君主制的

root: 希腊 monarkhikos「君主的」= monarkhes「唯一统治者」+ -ikos（形容词后缀，拉丁作 -icus）；monarkhes 出自 monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」。英语 monarchic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to a person, a system, a political stance, a manner, an org chart, a state, a domineering habit and a historical era.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用到人、制度、政治立场、作风、组织图、国家、专断习性与一个历史时代上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an org chart whose top box is a crown and whose every arrow converges on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张架构图，顶端方框是王冠，所有箭头都汇向它。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the ruler and the ruler-like manner share one adjective.
branches.cn: 人：统治者与类似统治者的作风共享一个形容词。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a form of government, a state that uses it and the era it marks.
branches.cn: 制度：政府形式、采用它的国家，以及它所标记的时代。

branches.en: THE STANCE: to be monarchic is to take the crown's side in a debate.
branches.cn: 立场：持 monarchic 立场就是在辩论中站在王冠一边。

branches.en: THE ORG CHART: one signature outweighs a whole committee.
branches.cn: 组织图：一个签名重于整个委员会。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a small tyrant can reign inside an office.
branches.cn: 习性：小暴君也能在办公室里临朝。

intro.en: Monarchic is a Greek compound plus the adjective suffix -ikos, and all three parts recur in English, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: monarchic 是希腊复合词加形容词后缀 -ikos，三部分都在英语中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek monos and arkhein give monarch and monarchy; -ikos, Latin -icus, gives monarchic and hierarchical.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 monos 与 arkhein 衍生 monarch 与 monarchy；-ikos（拉丁 -icus）衍生 monarchic 与 hierarchical。

items.example: The element also appears in monologue.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 中。

items.example: The root links rule to taking the lead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把统治与领头联系起来。

items.example: A monarkhes held the throne by birth.
items.exampleCN: 唯一统治者凭出生取得王位。

items.example: The suffix turns a ruler into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把统治者转为形容词。

items.example: The monarchic title passed to the son.
The monarchical system endured.
He ruled monarchically over the department.
items.exampleCN: 他像君主一样统治这个部门。

items.example: The monarchy fell after the war.
The monarch spoke briefly.

items.meaning: rule by priests, later ranked order
items.meaningCN: 祭司统治，后指等级秩序
items.example: The hierarchy was rigid.

latinEntries.structure: monarchicus, monarchica, monarchicum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 实验室器材；实验室器具与装置的总称
definition_en: the tools, instruments, vessels and consumable supplies needed to carry out work in a laboratory
core_image: 一条长实验台上排开烧杯、试管、滴管与一台离心机，桌下堆着未拆封的手套和离心管盒
scene: 生物教室里，学生把烧杯、试管和滴管一排摆上实验台，又在桌角放下一台离心机，桌下还堆着未拆封的手套。 The laboratory equipment for the water test filled two long benches.
sceneCN: 这里 laboratory equipment 指「实验室里成套使用的器具与装置」（第 1 个义项：实验室工作所需器材的总称）；句意为这次水质检测的实验室器材占满了两条长实验台。图中可辨识物件：烧杯、试管、滴管、离心机、手套盒。

pos.zh: 实验室器材；实验室器具与装置的总称（多作不可数）

senses.title: The whole stock of gear in a lab
senses.titleCN: 实验室全部器材的总称
senses.definition: the full set of tools and devices used to carry out laboratory work, taken as one mass
senses.definitionCN: 把实验室工作所用的工具与装置作为一个整体来看的总称
senses.example: The laboratory equipment for the water test filled two long benches.
senses.exampleCN: 这次水质检测的实验室器材占满了两条长实验台。
senses.why: The phrase names a category rather than a single object, so it works like a mass noun for everything a bench needs.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是一个类别而非单件物品，因此它像不可数名词一样涵盖一条实验台所需的全部东西。

senses.title: Glassware as a class
senses.definition: the glass vessels of a lab, such as beakers, flasks, tubes and pipettes
senses.definitionCN: 实验室里的玻璃容器，如烧杯、烧瓶、试管与移液管
senses.example: Most of the laboratory equipment in that cupboard is heat-resistant glassware.
senses.exampleCN: 那个柜子里的实验室器材大多是耐热玻璃器皿。
senses.why: Glass is the oldest and most familiar part of the stock, so it often stands for the whole in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 玻璃器皿是这套器材里最古老也最熟悉的部分，日常说法里常以它代指全体。

senses.title: Instruments and analysers
senses.definition: the powered or precision devices that measure, separate or analyse samples
senses.definitionCN: 对样品进行测量、分离或分析的电动或精密装置
senses.example: The new laboratory equipment includes a centrifuge and a spectrometer.
senses.exampleCN: 新到的实验室器材包括一台离心机和一台光谱仪。
senses.why: As labs grew mechanised, machines became the expensive core of the stock, and the phrase shifted toward them.
senses.whyCN: 随着实验室机械化，机器成了这套器材中昂贵的大件，短语的重心也随之偏向它们。

senses.title: Consumables and protection
senses.definition: the supplies that are used up or worn, such as gloves, tubes and reagents
senses.definitionCN: 会被用掉或磨损的用品，如手套、离心管与试剂
senses.example: Gloves and sample tubes are counted as laboratory equipment in the annual order.
senses.exampleCN: 手套与样品管在年度采购里被算作实验室器材。
senses.why: Budgets treat everything a bench burns through as equipment, because it must be bought again and again.
senses.whyCN: 预算把实验台消耗掉的一切都算作器材，因为它们必须反复采购。

senses.title: A matched kit for one procedure
senses.titleCN: 为一套流程配齐的成套器材
senses.definition: a set of items assembled to work together for a particular procedure
senses.definitionCN: 为某一特定流程组装起来、彼此配套的一组物件
senses.example: The soil-testing laboratory equipment came in one locked case.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤检测的实验室器材装在一只带锁的箱子里。
senses.why: The phrase can name a purposeful subset, not only the whole room: what one procedure needs, fitted together.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也可指有目的的一个子集，而不只是整间实验室：某一流程所需之物被配成一套。

senses.title: The institutional stock and its cost
senses.titleCN: 机构层面的装备与开支
senses.definition: the apparatus owned by an institution and the money and upkeep it requires
senses.definitionCN: 机构所拥有的器材以及维持它所需的经费与维护
senses.example: Cutting the laboratory equipment budget delayed three student projects.
senses.exampleCN: 削减实验室器材预算使三个学生项目延期。
senses.why: Once equipment is owned by a department it becomes a line in a budget, and the phrase takes on that administrative sense.
senses.whyCN: 器材一旦归某系所有，就成了预算里的一行，短语也就带上这层管理含义。

senses.title: A classroom set for teaching
senses.titleCN: 课堂演示与教学用的一套器材
senses.definition: the simplified set of apparatus provided for students to perform set exercises
senses.definitionCN: 供学生完成规定练习使用的简化器材组合
senses.example: The school bought laboratory equipment sturdy enough for first-year students.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采购的实验室器材结实得足以让一年级学生使用。
senses.why: Teaching sets are chosen for safety and repetition rather than precision, which makes them a distinct kind of stock.
senses.whyCN: 教学套件按安全与耐用挑选，而非按精度，因此构成一类不同的器材。

senses.title: A researcher's working kit
senses.titleCN: 研究者的方法储备（比喻）
senses.definition: used figuratively for the set of methods and tools a researcher has learned to rely on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻研究者已经学会依赖的一整套方法与工具
senses.example: Statistical modelling became part of her laboratory equipment long before she had a lab.
senses.exampleCN: 早在拥有实验室之前，统计建模就已成了她的「实验器材」。
senses.why: The abstract use treats trained methods as instruments that one carries into any problem.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法把训练有素的方法当作可以带进任何问题的器械。

intro.en: Two words meet in this phrase. The first goes back to Latin laborare 'to work'; the second goes back through French to a Norse verb for fitting out a ship. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个词合成。前者可追溯到拉丁语表示「劳作」的动词；后者经法语追溯到诺斯语中表示「装备船只」的动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Laborare 'to work, toil' came from labor 'work, effort'. The deeper origin of labor is not established, and suggestions linking it to a verb meaning 'to totter' are hypotheses only.
items.cn: laborare 意为「劳作、辛劳」，来自 labor「劳动、辛苦」。labor 的更深来源未得到证明，把它与某个意为「摇晃」的动词相联系的看法只是假说。

items.en: A laboratorium was a place for work, and by the Middle Ages the word was applied specifically to the workshop of an alchemist or apothecary.
items.cn: laboratorium 本指干活的地方，到中世纪专指炼金术士或药剂师的作坊。

items.en: English adopted laboratory in the sixteenth century from the medieval Latin form; an older variant, elaboratory, was used for chemical workshops.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从中世纪拉丁形式吸收了这个词；更早的变体 elaboratory 曾用于指化学作坊。

items.en: The second word goes back to Old French esquiper 'to fit out a ship', from Old Norse skipa 'to arrange, equip a ship', related to skip 'ship'.
items.cn: 第二个词可追溯到古法语 esquiper「装备船只」，来自诺斯语 skipa「安排、装备船只」，与表示「船」的词相关。

items.en: In English equip first meant 'to furnish with what is needed'; equipment named the act of fitting out before it named the things provided.
items.cn: 在英语中，equip 最初意为「配备所需之物」；equipment 先指配备这一行为，后指被配备出来的东西。

items.en: The two words became a fixed phrase with the growth of institutional science in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. First date uncertain: the exact year the phrase became standard is not recorded.
items.cn: 随着十九、二十世纪机构化科学的发展，这两个词结合成固定短语。首见年代不确定：该短语成为通行说法的确切年份没有记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but belong to other roots; group two holds the ordinary terms for laboratory gear.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近但词根不同的词；第二组是实验室器具的常用说法。

entries.definition: A room for washing, built on Latin lavare 'to wash'; it looks like laboratory but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指盥洗室，建立在拉丁语表示「洗」的动词上；外形像 laboratory，但与它没有共同词根。

entries.definition: An obsolete word for a chemical workshop; it looks like a longer form of laboratory but belonged to an older layer of usage.
entries.definitionCN: 指化学作坊的旧词；看起来像 laboratory 的更长形式，实则属于更早的用法层。

entries.definition: From the same ship-fitting verb, but it names a set of carriage horses or a retinue rather than laboratory gear.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「装备船只」的动词，但它指一套拉车的马或随从，而非实验室器具。

entries.definition: The verb means to furnish with what is needed; equipment is the resulting stock, so the two differ in word class only.
entries.definitionCN: 这个动词意为配备所需之物；equipment 是配备出来的存量，两者只差词性。

entries.definition: A formal collective noun for the equipment of a particular activity, often suggesting a connected set of parts.
entries.definitionCN: 某一活动所用器材的正式集合名词，常暗示一套彼此相连的部件。

entries.definition: A single device made for measuring or doing something delicate; it is one member of the larger stock.
entries.definitionCN: 为测量或做精细工作而制的单件装置；它是整套器材中的一员。

entries.definition: The glass vessels of a lab taken as a class; it covers beakers and flasks but not machines.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类统称的实验室玻璃容器；涵盖烧杯与烧瓶，但不含机器。

entries.definition: The expendable goods a lab uses up, such as gloves and reagents; equipment can be kept, supplies cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室会用尽的消耗品，如手套与试剂；器材可以留存，耗材则不能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase splits into a place of work and a verb for fitting out, so it means the things a workplace is fitted out with.
normal.cn: 这个短语可拆成「劳作之地」与「配备」两部分，因此指一个工作场所被配备出来的那些东西。

normal.en: The second word began with ships: to equip was to fit out a vessel before it was to fit out a bench.
normal.cn: 第二个词最初与船有关：配备原指把一条船装备齐全，后来才用于实验台。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the administrative life of the stock: equipment list, equipment room, equipment budget.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这套器材的管理轨迹：器材清单、器材室、器材预算。

normal.en: The family runs equip, equipped, equipment, equipage, re-equip, all from the fitting-out verb.
normal.cn: 同族词包括配备、已配备的、设备、成套用具、重新装备，都出自那个「装备」动词。

normal.en: A lab bench is read in layers: glass in front, instruments behind, consumables underneath.
normal.cn: 实验台可以分层来读：前排玻璃器皿，后排仪器，台下耗材。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's hold being packed for a long voyage, every item checked against a list.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船的货舱正为远航被打点，每件东西都对着清单核过。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen whose drawers were filled by someone who knew every recipe in advance.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，抽屉是被一个事先知道所有菜谱的人填满的。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller who carries a small case that opens into a whole workshop.
abstract.cn: 想象一位旅人带着一只小箱子，打开就是整间作坊。

examples.en: Every piece of laboratory equipment must be logged after use.
examples.cn: 每件实验室器材使用后都必须登记。

examples.en: The department replaced its old laboratory equipment with digital meters.
examples.cn: 该系用数字仪表替换了旧的实验室器材。

examples.en: Students learn to clean laboratory equipment before they run any test.
examples.cn: 学生在做任何检测之前先要学会清理实验室器材。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「干活的地方 + 配备」：为劳作之地配齐的一整套家当 → 实验室器材

root: laboratory 来自中世纪拉丁 laboratorium「干活的地方」，词根为拉丁 laborare「劳作」，labor 更深来源不确定；equipment 经古法语 esquiper「装备船只」上溯诺斯语 skipa，本义为把船配备齐全，后泛指配备出来的东西。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the whole stock of a lab to its glass, its machines, its consumables, a matched kit, an institutional budget line, a classroom set, and finally a researcher's trained methods.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实验室的全部器材，依次移到玻璃器皿、仪器、耗材、成套配件、机构预算项、课堂套件，最后到研究者训练有素的方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long bench loaded with glass, steel and boxes, everything a day's work requires.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长实验台，摆满玻璃、钢铁与盒子，一天工作所需的一切都在上面。

branches.en: Stock and ledger: the same mass of gear seen once on the bench and once in a budget.
branches.cn: 存量与账目：同一批器材，一次看在实验台上，一次看在预算里。

branches.en: Two materials of the bench: vessels of glass in front, instruments of steel behind.
branches.cn: 实验台的两种材料：前排玻璃器皿，后排钢铁仪器。

branches.en: What is used up and what is fitted together: gloves vanish, a test kit stays assembled.
branches.cn: 用尽之物与配好之物：手套会用完，检测套件则保持成套。

branches.en: The teaching version: the same stock simplified for young hands and repeated lessons.
branches.cn: 教学版本：同一套器材为年轻的手与反复的课而简化。

branches.en: The kit one carries: methods become instruments that travel with the researcher.
branches.cn: 随身的那套：方法成了随研究者移动的器械。

intro.en: Both halves of the phrase are built from ordinary morphemes, and each half also supports a small family of English words.
intro.cn: 短语的两半都由寻常语素构成，每一半还各自支撑一小族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin laborare and laboratorium stand behind the first word; the second comes from French and Norse rather than Latin, so the phrase mixes two lineages.
latinIntro.cn: 第一个词背后是拉丁语的劳作动词与工作场所名词；第二个词来自法语与诺斯语而非拉丁语，因此这个短语混合了两条血脉。

items.example: The laboratory is where the stock is kept.
items.exampleCN: 实验室就是这套器材存放的地方。

items.example: The first word begins with the idea of work itself.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词从「劳作」这一观念开始。

items.meaning: a place where something is done
items.example: The suffix turns a verb of working into a name for the workplace.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「劳作」动词变成工作场所之名。

items.structure: Old French esquiper, from Old Norse skipa
items.example: To equip a bench is the same gesture as fitting out a ship.
items.exampleCN: 装备一张实验台，与把一条船配备齐全，是同一个动作。

items.meaning: the things provided for an activity
items.meaningCN: 为某项活动提供的东西
items.example: The noun turns the act of fitting out into the stock itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把配备的行为转为配备出来的存量。

items.example: A well-equipped lab is one whose stock is complete.
items.exampleCN: 装备良好的实验室，就是器材齐备的实验室。

items.example: Old benches are re-equipped rather than replaced.
items.exampleCN: 旧实验台是重新装备，而不是整台换掉。

items.example: The fixed phrase joins the place to what fills it.
items.exampleCN: 这个固定短语把场所与填满它的东西接在一起。

items.meaning: describing a room, list or budget for such gear
items.meaningCN: 描述器材室、清单或预算的
items.example: The hyphenated form works as a modifier before another noun.
items.exampleCN: 带连字符的形式在另一名词前作修饰语。

definition_en: the condition, policy or ideology in which several cultures coexist and are officially recognized
core_image: 一张长桌上并排放着好几本不同文字的同一份文件，每一本都盖着同样的公章
scene: 一份省级文件把多种文化共存写成官方立场，会议室里摆着好几种语言的译本， The province adopted multiculturalism as official policy in the nineteen seventies.
sceneCN: 这里 multiculturalism 指「以官方政策形式承认并支持多种文化的制度安排」（第 2 个义项：国家或省级政策）；句意为该省在二十世纪七十年代把多元文化主义定为官方政策。图中可辨识物件：长桌、多语译本、公章、政策文件。

senses.title: The coexistence of several cultures
senses.definition: the condition in which several cultures live side by side in one society
senses.definitionCN: 多种文化在同一社会中并存的状况
senses.example: Multiculturalism is a fact of the city before it is a policy.
senses.exampleCN: 在这座城市里，多元文化先是事实，然后才成为政策。
senses.why: The suffix turns the adjective into a noun of condition: what was a description of a place now names the state of that place.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把形容词变成表示状态的名词：原本描述地点的说法，现在命名那个地点的状态。

senses.title: An official policy supporting several cultures
senses.titleCN: 支持多种文化的官方政策
senses.definition: a government policy that recognizes and supports the cultures of different groups
senses.definitionCN: 承认并支持不同群体文化的政府政策
senses.example: The province adopted multiculturalism as official policy in the nineteen seventies.
senses.exampleCN: 该省在二十世纪七十年代把多元文化主义定为官方政策。
senses.why: Once a state funds language classes and heritage festivals, the condition becomes an instrument of government.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家资助语言课程与遗产节庆，这种状态就变成治理工具。

senses.title: An ideology that values difference
senses.definition: the belief that cultural differences should be preserved and valued rather than melted away
senses.definitionCN: 认为文化差异应被保留和重视、而非被熔化的信念
senses.example: Multiculturalism insists that difference is a public good, not a problem to be solved.
senses.exampleCN: 多元文化主义坚持差异是一种公共善，而不是待解决的问题。
senses.why: Policy needs a theory behind it, so the same word also names the belief that gives the policy its justification.
senses.whyCN: 政策背后需要理论，因此同一个词也命名那套为政策提供理由的信念。

senses.title: A social movement for recognition
senses.definition: the movement through which minority groups seek public recognition of their cultures
senses.definitionCN: 少数群体争取其文化获得公共承认的运动
senses.example: Multiculturalism grew out of movements that demanded a place in the school curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 多元文化主义源自那些要求在课程中占有一席之地的运动。
senses.why: The noun can name actors as well as ideas: people organized to make the condition visible and the policy possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既可指观念，也可指行动者：人们组织起来，让这种状态被看见，也让政策成为可能。

senses.title: An educational approach
senses.definition: an approach in schools that includes the histories and cultures of several groups
senses.definitionCN: 在学校中纳入多个群体历史与文化的教育取向
senses.example: Multiculturalism in the classroom changed which poets were read.
senses.exampleCN: 课堂里的多元文化主义改变了学生读哪些诗人的作品。
senses.why: Schools are where a society decides what the next generation will inherit, so the doctrine quickly becomes a curriculum question.
senses.whyCN: 学校是社会决定下一代继承什么的地方，因此这套主张很快变成课程问题。

senses.title: A demographic description
senses.definition: a neutral description of a society composed of several cultural groups
senses.definitionCN: 对由多个文化群体组成的社会的中性描述
senses.example: Census reports use multiculturalism to describe the changing suburbs.
senses.exampleCN: 人口普查报告用多元文化主义来描述不断变化的郊区。
senses.why: The word can be stripped of ideology and used as a plain count: several cultures are present, and that is all it says.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以剥离意识形态，只作平实计数：这里存在多种文化，如此而已。

senses.title: A label used by critics
senses.definition: the word as used by opponents who blame it for fragmentation or for treating groups as separate
senses.definitionCN: 反对者用它指责社会碎片化、或把群体当作彼此隔离的标签
senses.example: The minister blamed multiculturalism for the decline of a shared public life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部长把公共生活的衰退归咎于多元文化主义。
senses.why: A policy that protects difference can be accused of producing separation, so the same noun becomes a term of attack.
senses.whyCN: 保护差异的政策可能被指控制造隔阂，于是同一个名词变成攻击用语。

senses.title: Mixing traditions in art and media
senses.titleCN: 艺术与媒体中混合多种传统
senses.definition: an artistic practice that deliberately combines forms from several cultural traditions
senses.definitionCN: 有意把多种文化传统的形式结合起来的艺术实践
senses.example: The film's multiculturalism is visible in its mixed score and subtitles.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片的多元文化主义体现在混编配乐与字幕上。
senses.why: The doctrine of many cultures becomes a style when artists let traditions meet inside one work.
senses.whyCN: 当艺术家让多种传统在一件作品里相遇，这套「多文化」主张就变成一种风格。

intro.en: Multiculturalism is multicultural plus -ism, the suffix for doctrines and movements, which reached English through Latin from Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: multiculturalism 是 multicultural 加 -ism 构成，后者是表示学说与运动的后缀，经拉丁语从希腊语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Multus, many, supplied the combining prefix multi-, which English uses freely in modern compounds.
items.cn: multus 意为「多」，提供组合前缀 multi-，英语在现代复合词中自由使用它。

items.en: Cultura, tilling and care, gave culture and cultural; the culture here is the learned way of life, not the field.
items.cn: cultura 意为耕作与照料，给出 culture 与 cultural；这里的 culture 指习得的生活方式，而非田地。

items.en: Greek -ismos named a practice or doctrine and passed through Latin -ismus into English -ism, which builds socialism, realism and multiculturalism alike.
items.cn: 希腊语 -ismos 指某种实践或学说，经拉丁语 -ismus 进入英语 -ism，同样构成 socialism（社会主义）、realism（写实主义）与 multiculturalism。

items.en: The noun appeared in the mid twentieth century as migration made several cultures a permanent public fact in industrial cities.
items.cn: 这个名词在二十世纪中叶出现，当时移民使多种文化成为工业城市里长期的公共事实。

items.en: Canada adopted an official multiculturalism policy in the early nineteen seventies, and Australia followed soon after, turning the word into a label of state policy.
items.cn: 加拿大在二十世纪七十年代初采纳官方多元文化政策，澳大利亚随后跟进，把这个词变成国家政策的标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the noun and the exact date of its adoption as policy are reported differently, so both should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个名词在英语中的最早使用、以及它被采纳为政策的确切日期，各家记载不一，两者都应视为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same stock that are easily confused; the second holds doctrines or descriptions of plural societies.
note.cn: 第一组是同源、极易混淆的词；第二组是关于多元社会的学说或描述。

entries.definition: Describing a place or design that contains several cultures; multiculturalism is the noun for the condition, policy or doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 描述包含多种文化的地点或设计；multiculturalism 是表示状态、政策或学说的名词。

entries.definition: A supporter of multiculturalism; the -ist form names a person, not the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 多元文化主义的支持者；带 -ist 的形式指人，不指学说。

entries.definition: An approach that explains human behaviour mainly by culture; it lacks the many-prefix and is not a policy label.
entries.definitionCN: 主要用文化解释人类行为的取向；它没有表示「多」的前缀，也不是政策标签。

entries.definition: A policy or approach stressing exchange and interaction between cultures rather than their parallel existence.
entries.definitionCN: 强调文化之间的交流与互动、而非平行共存的政策或取向。

entries.definition: The acceptance of many groups or viewpoints in one society; broader than multiculturalism, which focuses on culture.
entries.definitionCN: 接受一个社会中存在多个群体或观点；比聚焦文化的 multiculturalism 更宽。

entries.definition: The presence of variety; it can be cultural, biological or organizational, and carries no programme by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 存在多样性；可以是文化的、生物的和组织的，本身不携带纲领。

entries.definition: The view that all people belong to one worldwide community; it stresses openness to the world, not the protection of separate cultures.
entries.definitionCN: 认为所有人都属于同一个世界共同体的观点；它强调对世界开放，而非保护彼此分隔的文化。

entries.definition: The process by which minority groups are absorbed into the dominant culture; it is the policy multiculturalism often defines itself against.
entries.definitionCN: 少数群体被吸收进主流文化的过程；它常是多元文化主义用来定义自身对立面的政策。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real doctrine suffix, the real family and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示学说的真实后缀、真实的同族词，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: multicultural plus the doctrine suffix: the same ending builds realism and socialism, so the word names a programme, not a count.
normal.cn: multicultural 加表示学说的后缀：同一词尾也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义），因此这个词命名一套纲领，而不是一次计数。

normal.en: The family runs multicultural, multiculturalism, multiculturalist and multiculturalistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 multicultural（多元文化的）、multiculturalism（多元文化主义）、multiculturalist（多元文化主义者）、multiculturalistic（带多元文化主义色彩的）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: official multiculturalism, state multiculturalism, the multiculturalism debate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：官方多元文化主义、国家多元文化主义、关于多元文化主义的争论。

normal.en: The word became official in Canada and Australia in the nineteen seventies.
normal.cn: 这个词在二十世纪七十年代于加拿大与澳大利亚成为官方用语。

normal.en: Its usual rival in policy debate is assimilation, not diversity.
normal.cn: 在政策争论中，它通常的对手是同化，而不是多样性。

abstract.en: Picture several books of law bound in one cover, each in a different script.
abstract.cn: 想象好几本法律文本装进同一个封面，每本用不同文字。

abstract.en: Picture a choir in which every section sings a different melody and none is asked to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，每个声部唱不同旋律，却没有一个被要求停下。

abstract.en: Picture a map with many coloured regions and no single colour allowed to cover the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有许多色块，没有任何一种颜色被允许盖满整页。

examples.en: Multiculturalism changed the language of citizenship in the late twentieth century.
examples.cn: 多元文化主义在二十世纪后期改变了公民身份的话语。

examples.en: The city's multiculturalism is older than its official policy.
examples.cn: 这座城市的多元文化比它的官方政策更早存在。

examples.en: Critics argue that multiculturalism can harden the boundaries it meant to soften.
examples.cn: 批评者认为，多元文化主义可能反而硬化了它本想软化的边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「多」加「文化的」再加「主义」——把许多种文化共存写成一套主张，就是多元文化主义。

root: 由 multicultural 加表示学说与运动的后缀 -ism 构成。multi- 来自拉丁语 multus「多」，cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，-ism 经拉丁语 -ismus 源自希腊语 -ismos。colere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one doctrine through its life: a condition, a policy, an ideology, a movement, a school subject, a census line, a term of attack and finally an artistic style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一套主张的生命史展开：先是状态，再是政策、意识形态、运动、学校课程、人口普查条目、攻击用语，最后是艺术风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several scripts sharing one seal, each text officially equal.
core.cn: 核心意象：几种文字共享同一枚印章，每份文本在官方意义上平等。

branches.en: FACT AND COUNT: coexistence can be described neutrally, as a census describes a population.
branches.cn: 事实与计数：共存可以被中性描述，就像人口普查描述人口那样。

branches.en: POLICY: the state turns coexistence into budgets, language classes and heritage festivals.
branches.cn: 政策：国家把共存变成预算、语言课程与遗产节庆。

branches.en: DOCTRINE AND MOVEMENT: a belief justifies the policy, and organized groups push it forward.
branches.cn: 学说与运动：信念为政策提供理由，组织起来的群体则推动它。

branches.en: SCHOOLING: the curriculum decides which cultures the next generation will inherit.
branches.cn: 学校教育：课程决定下一代继承哪些文化。

branches.en: ATTACK AND STYLE: opponents turn the word into blame, while artists turn it into mixed forms.
branches.cn: 攻击与风格：反对者把这个词变成指责，艺术家则把它变成混合形式。

intro.en: Multiculturalism is a many-prefix, a culture stem, an adjective ending and a doctrine suffix in one word.
intro.cn: multiculturalism 由一个表示「多」的前缀、一个 culture 词干、一个形容词词尾与一个表示学说的后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin multus and cultura supply the first two parts, -alis makes the adjective, and -ismus, from Greek -ismos, makes the doctrine noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 multus 与 cultura 提供前两部分，-alis 构成形容词，来自希腊语 -ismos 的 -ismus 则构成表示学说的名词。

items.structure: multi- (Latin combining form of multus, many)
items.example: The prefix also builds multilingual and multiethnic.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也构成 multilingual（多语的）与 multiethnic（多族裔的）。

items.example: The noun became English culture through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词经法语成为英语 culture。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

items.example: The city is multicultural.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市是多元文化的。

items.example: The same ending builds realism and socialism.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 realism（写实主义）与 socialism（社会主义）。

items.meaning: the policy or doctrine of several cultures
items.meaningCN: 多种文化的政策或学说
items.example: Official multiculturalism began in the nineteen seventies.
items.exampleCN: 官方多元文化主义始于二十世纪七十年代。

items.meaningCN: 多元文化主义的支持者
items.example: The multiculturalist defended the policy.
items.exampleCN: 这位多元文化主义者为政策辩护。

items.meaningCN: 带多元文化主义色彩的

items.exampleCN: 这份报告带有多元文化主义的语调。

items.meaning: a doctrine stressing exchange between cultures
items.meaningCN: 强调文化间交流的学说
items.example: Interculturalism stresses dialogue more than parallel lives.
items.exampleCN: 跨文化主义更强调对话，而非平行生活。

definition_zh: v. 宠爱，娇养；悉心照料
definition_en: to treat someone with too much care and attention
core_image: 奶奶把小猫裹进围巾，只露出一张脸
scene: 奶奶把那只小猫捧在怀里，天天宠着。 Grandmother cosseted the kitten every single day.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cosset 指宠爱；句意是奶奶天天宠着那只小猫。

senses.title: Pamper
senses.definition: to treat someone with great fondness
senses.definitionCN: 满怀宠爱地对待某人
senses.example: Grandmother cosseted the kitten.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶宠着那只小猫。

definition_zh: 按固定程序进行的一套仪式；也指仪式性的
definition_en: a set of actions performed in a fixed order, especially for religious or solemn purposes, and the adjective describing such actions
core_image: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，最年长的人先点上一炷香，其余人依次跟上
scene: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，家里最年长的人先点上一炷香。 The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
sceneCN: 这里 ritual 指「按固定程序进行的一套仪式」（第 1 个义项：有既定顺序的庄严动作）；句意为节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。可辨识物件：神龛、米碗、清水、香、钟。

senses.title: A set of actions in fixed order
senses.titleCN: 按固定顺序进行的一套动作
senses.definition: a sequence of actions repeated in the same order on the same kind of occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在同类场合按同样顺序重复的一连串动作
senses.example: The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
senses.exampleCN: 节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。
senses.why: ritus named a religious rite, and the noun keeps the idea of an order that must not be varied.
senses.whyCN: ritus 指宗教仪式，这个名词保留了「顺序不可更改」的意思。

senses.title: The ordered rites of worship
senses.definition: the prescribed words and gestures of a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 宗教礼拜中规定的言辞与动作
senses.example: The priest followed the ritual exactly, down to the last bow.
senses.exampleCN: 司仪严格遵循仪式，连最后一次鞠躬也不差。
senses.why: religion is where fixed order is felt to be most necessary, so the word grew strong there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教最能感到固定顺序的必要，这个词也在此处扎根最深。

senses.title: A personal daily routine
senses.definition: a small repeated sequence that marks a part of the day, such as coffee before work
senses.definitionCN: 标记一天中某段时间的重复小序列，如上班前的咖啡
senses.example: Her morning ritual is a cup of tea and ten minutes of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的晨间固定程序是一杯茶和十分钟的安静。
senses.why: the word moved from the altar to the kitchen because both need a dependable order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从祭坛移到厨房，因为两者都需要可靠的顺序。

senses.title: Stylized social courtesy
senses.titleCN: 社会交往中的程式化礼节
senses.definition: the expected words and gestures of greeting, toasting or taking leave
senses.definitionCN: 问候、敬酒或告别时所期待的言辞与动作
senses.example: Their greeting was a ritual of three bows and two questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的问候是一套三鞠躬加两个问题的礼节。
senses.why: social life repeats its own small liturgies, and the same noun covers them.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活重复着自己的小礼序，同一个名词也就涵盖了它们。

senses.title: Rites marking a change of status
senses.titleCN: 标记身份转变的过渡仪式
senses.definition: ceremonies such as birth rites, initiation or funerals that move a person from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 出生礼、成年礼或葬礼等把人从一种状态转入另一种状态的仪式
senses.example: The initiation ritual lasted three days and ended with a new name.
senses.exampleCN: 成年仪式持续三天，最后以一个新名字结束。
senses.why: anthropology found that the most important rituals mark a crossing, not a repetition.
senses.whyCN: 人类学发现最重要的仪式标记的是跨越，而非重复。

senses.title: Repetition that has become compulsive
senses.titleCN: 仪式化的重复行为（心理层面）
senses.definition: a repeated act that calms anxiety or must be performed to avoid distress
senses.definitionCN: 为安抚焦虑而重复、或必须执行以避免痛苦的动作
senses.example: He developed a private ritual of checking the lock four times.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了一个私下的仪式：把锁检查四次。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion has the same outward shape as rite.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上相同。

senses.title: Symbolic acts that bind a group
senses.definition: public gestures such as flag-raising or oath-taking that make a group feel itself
senses.definitionCN: 升旗或宣誓等让群体感到自身存在的公开动作
senses.example: The school's Monday ritual assembled every class on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 学校周一的仪式把每个班都召集到操场上。
senses.why: a group needs a body, and repeated gestures give it one.
senses.whyCN: 群体需要一个形体，而重复的动作提供了这个形体。

senses.title: Ritual as an adjective
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of, or used in, a rite'
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示「仪式的」或「仪式中使用的」
senses.example: The ritual dance is performed only by the elders.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仪式之舞只由长者表演。
senses.why: the adjective is simply the noun doing modifying work, a common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是名词在起修饰作用，这是英语常见的转用。

senses.title: A fixed routine that feels obligatory
senses.titleCN: 例行公事般的固定做法
senses.definition: a practice repeated so often that it has lost its original purpose
senses.definitionCN: 重复得太频繁、已失去原初目的的做法
senses.example: The weekly meeting had become a ritual nobody questioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会已成了一套无人质疑的例行程序。
senses.why: when order outlives meaning, the word turns slightly ironic.
senses.whyCN: 当顺序比意义活得更久，这个词就带上了一点讽刺。

intro.en: Ritual comes from Latin ritualis 'relating to rites', from ritus 'a rite, a religious ceremony', through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritual 经古法语来自拉丁 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，而 ritualis 出自 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony, a custom'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼、惯例」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与吠陀语中表示「固定秩序」的词相联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis made a relational adjective, so ritualis meant 'belonging to a rite' and covered both books and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 ritualis 意为「属于仪式的」，书籍与动作都可用它形容。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective and noun into English, where ritual first named a book of church rites.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词与名词带入英语，ritual 最初指记载教会礼仪的书。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun meant the rites themselves, and by the nineteenth it had spread to social and personal practice.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，名词已指礼仪本身；到十九世纪，又扩展到社会与个人实践。

items.en: Both disciplines adopted the word, one for rites of passage and the other for compulsive repetition.
items.cn: 人类学与心理学都采用了这个词，前者指过渡仪式，后者指强迫性重复。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of ritus is unsettled, and the earliest use of the ironic 'mere routine' sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ritus 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，讽刺性的「只是例行公事」义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stem; group two holds terms for related solemn or repeated practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关庄严或重复做法的词。

entries.definition: One prescribed ceremony, usually religious or solemn; ritual can name the whole ordered system or the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼，通常宗教或庄严；ritual 可指整套有序体系或风格。

entries.definition: Describes something done in the manner of a rite, often with a hint of excess.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以仪式方式完成的事物，常带过度拘泥的暗示。

entries.definition: Excessive attachment to rites, or the study of them as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式的过度依附，或把仪式当作体系来研究。

entries.definition: To turn an action into a rite or to perform it in a fixed ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个动作变成仪式，或以固定礼仪方式完成。

entries.definition: A formal event with a set order; it stresses occasion and dignity more than repeated practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指有固定顺序的正式活动；比「反复实践」更强调场合与庄重。

entries.definition: The prescribed form of public religious worship, usually written down for a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 指公共宗教礼拜的规定形式，通常为会众写成文本。

entries.definition: The act of keeping a law, feast or custom; it names compliance rather than the sequence of acts.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵守法律、节期或习俗；它指遵从，而非动作序列。

entries.definition: An ordinary repeated way of doing things, without the solemn charge that ritual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指平常重复的做事方式，不带 ritual 那种庄严意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritus 'rite' plus -alis 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to a rite'.
normal.cn: ritus「仪式」加 -alis「属于……的」，得到「属于仪式的」。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: religious ritual, daily ritual, morning ritual, ritual dance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：宗教仪式、每日固定程序、晨间固定程序、仪式之舞。

normal.en: Anthropology links ritual to rites of passage: a crossing is marked, not merely repeated.
normal.cn: 人类学把仪式与过渡礼仪相连：被标记的是跨越，而不只是重复。

normal.en: The ironic sense appears when a routine outlives its reason, as in a meeting that is a ritual.
normal.cn: 当惯例活得比理由更久，讽刺义就出现，如「一场纯属仪式的会议」。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step must be taken in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级都必须按同样顺序踏过。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that rings not to tell time but to make time feel real.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，它响不是为了报时，而是让时间显得真实。

abstract.en: Picture a door that only opens when three hands touch it in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有三只手依次触碰才会打开。

examples.en: The harvest ritual begins with the youngest child pouring water.
examples.cn: 丰收仪式由最小的孩子倒水开始。

examples.en: Modern offices have their own rituals of greeting and leaving.
examples.cn: 现代办公室有自己的问候与告别仪式。

examples.en: The therapist asked whether the ritual reduced his anxiety.
examples.cn: 治疗师问他这套仪式是否减轻了焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ri（日）+ tual」——每天按同一顺序做的事，就成了仪式

root: 拉丁 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」→ ritualis「与仪式有关的」→ 古法语 → 英语 ritual。ritus 的更深来源不确定，与吠陀语「固定秩序」词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one order: a sequence that must be repeated exactly, performed at an altar, in a kitchen, in a greeting, at a crossing, in a compulsion, on a flagpole and finally in an empty meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个顺序展开：一套必须照样重复的动作，依次在祭坛、厨房、问候、人生关口、强迫行为、旗杆前上演，最后落到一场空洞的会议上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bowls laid out in a fixed order, each filled only when the previous one is full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按固定次序摆好的碗，前一只满了才轮到下一只。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: first a sequence, then the adjective that labels anything belonging to it.
branches.cn: 顺序本身：先是动作序列，再是标记任何属于该序列之物的形容词。

branches.en: ALTAR AND CROSSING: worship repeats the order, while initiation uses it to move a person.
branches.cn: 祭坛与关口：礼拜重复顺序，成年礼则用顺序移动一个人。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND EMPTY MEETING: the same order comforts a morning and hollows out a schedule.
branches.cn: 厨房与空会：同一顺序既安抚一个早晨，也掏空一张日程。

branches.en: COURTESY AND FLAG: small greetings and public gestures both make a group hold together.
branches.cn: 礼节与旗帜：小小问候与公开动作都能让群体维系。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the shape of a rite appears without its meaning, and the repetition becomes a cage.
branches.cn: 强迫：仪式的形状还在，意义却已消失，重复变成牢笼。

intro.en: Ritual is a Latin noun stem with a relational suffix, and that stem also builds the shorter noun rite and the whole ritualistic family.
intro.cn: ritual 是一个拉丁名词词干加关系后缀，同一词干还构成较短的名词 rite 与整个 ritualistic 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus supplied the stem and -alis supplied the adjective ending; English later added -istic, -ism and -ize to build manner, system and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 提供词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾；英语后来加上 -istic、-ism 与 -ize，构成方式、体系与动词。

senses.title: Famous and respected
senses.definition: famous and respected in a particular profession
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）在某一专业领域有名望且受尊敬
senses.example: The eminent historian spent forty years on a single dynasty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位杰出的历史学家在一个王朝上花了四十年。

senses.exampleCN: 她出身于一个法官与外交官辈出的显赫家族。

intro.en: Eminent comes from Latin e- meaning out and minere meaning to jut; eminere is to stand out above the surroundings, like a peak above a range.
intro.cn: eminent 来自拉丁语 e-（向外）与 minere（突出）；eminere 意为高出周围，像一座山峰高出整片丘陵。

items.en: Minere means to jut or to project, and gives English prominent and imminent.

items.en: Eminere means to stand out, built from e- plus minere.
