definition_zh: 洪涝；淹没过程；城市内涝；大量涌入；满溢；进水
definition_en: the process or event of water covering land, or of an overwhelming quantity of things filling a place
core_image: 雨水在城市街道上积成一片浅海，井盖下翻涌，车灯在水面拉出长条倒影
scene: 连日暴雨让低洼的街区积水不退，校车无法通行。 Persistent flooding forced the school to close for a week.
sceneCN: 这里指「持续积水造成的洪涝现象」（第 1 个义项：地表被水覆盖的灾害过程）；句意为持续的洪涝迫使学校停课一周。图中可辨识物件：漫过路缘的积水、半没的车轮、翻涌的井口、关闭的校门。

pos.zh: 洪涝；淹没；大量涌入；满溢

senses.title: The event of water covering land
senses.titleCN: 地表被水覆盖的洪涝事件
senses.definition: the event or process in which water covers land that is normally dry
senses.definitionCN: 水覆盖通常干燥土地的事件或过程
senses.example: Persistent flooding forced the school to close for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 持续的洪涝迫使学校停课一周。
senses.why: The -ing form names the going-on of the event, so it suits reports, warnings and insurance.
senses.whyCN: 这一动名词形式命名事件的持续过程，因此适用于报告、警报与保险。

senses.title: A river overflowing its channel
senses.definition: the process by which a river or stream rises above its banks and spreads over the floodplain
senses.definitionCN: 河流或溪流涨过河岸、铺展到洪泛平原的过程
senses.example: River flooding began upstream and reached the town by nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 河流漫溢从上游开始，到傍晚抵达城镇。
senses.why: Hydrology needs a name for the process rather than for a single flood.
senses.whyCN: 水文学需要一个指过程而非单次洪水的名称。

senses.title: Urban flooding after heavy rain
senses.definition: the accumulation of rainwater in streets and underpasses when drainage cannot keep up
senses.definitionCN: 排水跟不上时，雨水在街道与地下通道积聚的现象
senses.example: Urban flooding stranded buses under the flyover.
senses.exampleCN: 城市内涝把公交车困在高架桥下。
senses.why: The word shifts from rivers to pavement: the cause is not a bank burst but a drain that is too small.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从河流转到路面：成因不是堤岸决口，而是排水口太小。

senses.title: An overwhelming inflow of goods or messages
senses.titleCN: 商品或信息的大量涌入
senses.definition: the arrival of so many goods, applications or messages that a system cannot absorb them
senses.definitionCN: 商品、申请或信息到来过多，使系统无法吸收
senses.example: The flooding of the market with cheap imports hurt local mills.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口商品大量涌入市场，打击了本地工厂。
senses.why: The water image survives in the metaphor: the system is a channel that has been overtopped.
senses.whyCN: 水的意象在比喻中保留：系统成了一条被漫过的渠道。

senses.title: Filling a place with light
senses.definition: the effect of light spreading through and filling a space
senses.definitionCN: 光在空间中铺开并充满的效果
senses.example: The flooding of the stage with white light erased every shadow.
senses.exampleCN: 白光涌满舞台，把所有阴影都抹掉了。
senses.why: Light and water share the behaviour of spreading until a boundary stops them.
senses.whyCN: 光与水共享同一种行为：不断铺开，直到边界拦住。

senses.title: An engine or carburettor taking in too much fuel
senses.titleCN: 发动机或化油器进液过多
senses.definition: the condition in which excess fuel or water enters an engine and prevents it from starting
senses.definitionCN: 过多燃料或水进入发动机、使其无法启动的状态
senses.example: Repeated short trips caused flooding in the carburettor.
senses.exampleCN: 反复短途行驶导致化油器进液过多。
senses.why: The technical sense treats the engine as a chamber that has been overfilled.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义把发动机视为被灌得过满的腔室。

senses.title: Being overwhelmed by emotion
senses.definition: a state in which strong feeling rises and leaves no room for thought
senses.definitionCN: 强烈情绪上涨、使思考再无空间的状态
senses.example: The flooding of grief came later, when the house was quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 悲伤的淹没来得更晚，在屋子安静下来之后。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the rise and the loss of room, with no water at all.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「上涨」与「没有余地」，完全不涉及水。

senses.title: Information overload
senses.definition: the condition of receiving far more information than one can process, as in a flooded feed
senses.definitionCN: 收到远超处理能力的信息的状态，如被灌满的信息流
senses.example: Constant flooding of the feed made the important notice invisible.
senses.exampleCN: 信息流不断被灌满，使那条重要通知变得看不见。
senses.why: Digital life reused the old image: a channel that carries too much ceases to carry anything.
senses.whyCN: 数字生活沿用旧意象：承载过多的渠道反而什么都传送不了。

intro.en: Flooding is flood plus the noun suffix -ing. The base is Old English flōd from Proto-Germanic *flōduz, and the suffix is the native English -ing that turns verbs into names for processes.
intro.cn: flooding 由 flood 加名词后缀 -ing 构成。词基是古英语 flōd，源自原始日耳曼 *flōduz；后缀是英语本族的 -ing，把动词转为过程名称。

items.en: The base flōd named rising water, and the derived verb flōdian already allowed a process noun in principle.
items.cn: 词基 flōd 指上涨的水，其派生动词 flōdian 原则上已可构成过程名词。

items.en: The native -ing suffix was fully productive in Middle English, forming nouns for ongoing actions and events.
items.cn: 本族 -ing 后缀在中古英语中已高度能产，可构成表示持续动作与事件的名词。

items.en: Modern hydrology and insurance gave flooding a technical standing as a measurable hazard rather than a single event.
items.cn: 现代水文学与保险业使 flooding 获得技术地位，成为可度量的灾害而非单次事件。

items.en: Twentieth-century planning produced fixed terms such as urban flooding, coastal flooding and flooding risk.
items.cn: 20 世纪的规划实践产生了城市内涝、沿海洪涝、洪涝风险等固定术语。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word was extended to overloaded information channels, keeping the water image.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，该词被扩展到过载的信息渠道，水的意象得以保留。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first written use of the -ing noun is not pinned down, though its formation is transparent and not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：该 -ing 名词最早的书证难以确定，但其构成方式透明，并无疑义。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb that differ in grammatical role; group two holds nouns for water disasters and for overwhelming inflows.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的不同语法形式；第二组是水灾与压倒性涌入的近义名词。

entries.definition: The base form: one body of water, or the act of covering land; it can be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 原形：一片水体，或淹没土地的动作；可以计数。

entries.definition: The completed state, as in a flooded road; it describes the result rather than the process.
entries.definitionCN: 完成状态，如被淹的道路；描述结果而非过程。

entries.definition: The flat land that flooding is expected to cover; the word names terrain, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会被洪涝覆盖的平地；该词指地形，而非事件。

entries.definition: A formal noun for the state of being covered by water; it is countable and often literary.
entries.definitionCN: 表示被水覆盖状态的正式名词；可计数，常带文学色彩。

entries.definition: Saturation of soil so that water cannot drain away; narrower than flooding, and usually about ground, not streets.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤饱和以致水无法排出；比 flooding 窄，通常指地面而非街道。

entries.definition: The spilling of water or anything else past a container's limit; it stresses the moment of exceeding capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 水或任何事物超出容器限度而溢出；强调超出容量的那一刻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base word, the real suffix and the real technical compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词基、真实的后缀与真实的技术复合词。

normal.en: Flood plus -ing: the base names the water, the suffix names the process.
normal.cn: flood 加 -ing：词基指水，后缀指过程。

normal.en: Hydrology prefers the -ing form because hazards are processes, not objects.
normal.cn: 水文学偏爱 -ing 形式，因为灾害是过程而不是物体。

normal.en: Fixed terms: urban flooding, coastal flooding, flash flooding.
normal.cn: 固定术语：城市内涝、沿海洪涝、突发性洪涝。

normal.en: The metaphorical use survives in flooding the market and flooding the feed.
normal.cn: 比喻用法保留在「商品涌满市场」与「信息流被灌满」中。

normal.en: The engine sense treats a chamber as overfilled.
normal.cn: 发动机义把腔室视为被灌得过满。

abstract.en: Picture a drain that is asked to carry a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被要求排走一条河的排水口。

abstract.en: Picture a screen where the important line is buried under a thousand others.
abstract.cn: 想象一块屏幕，重要的一行被上千行别的埋住。

abstract.en: Picture quiet returning to a house and grief arriving with it.
abstract.cn: 想象屋子重新安静下来，悲伤随之到来。

examples.en: Flooding closed the coastal road for two tides.
examples.cn: 洪涝使沿海公路连续两个潮汐无法通行。

examples.en: Engineers map flooding risk before approving new housing.
examples.cn: 工程师在批准新建住宅前先绘制洪涝风险图。

examples.en: The flooding of the archive with unsorted files slowed every search.
examples.cn: 未整理文件大量涌入档案库，使每次检索都变慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「flood（洪水）+ ing（进行）」——洪水正在进行 → 洪涝、淹没

root: 由 flood（古英语 flōd，原始日耳曼 *flōduz）+ 本族后缀 -ing 构成；词基与德语 Flut、荷兰语 vloed 同源，并经印欧 *pleu-「流动」与拉丁 pluere「下雨」远亲同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a process of exceeding a limit: water over land, drains over capacity, goods over a market, light over a stage, fuel over an engine and information over attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都命名「超出限度」的过程：水漫过土地、排水超过容量、商品涌过市场、光铺满舞台、燃料灌满发动机、信息超过注意力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface that keeps rising until the container it was meant to stay in is irrelevant.
core.cn: 核心意象：不断上涨的水面，直到原本该容纳它的容器形同虚设。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: a single event and a river's seasonal behaviour are the same noun at two scales.
branches.cn: 过程：单次事件与河流的季节性行为，是同一名词的两种尺度。

branches.en: PAVEMENT: when the drain is too small, streets behave like river banks.
branches.cn: 路面：当排水口太小，街道就像河岸。

branches.en: INFLOW: goods and messages become water that overfills a channel.
branches.cn: 涌入：商品与信息变成灌满渠道的水。

branches.en: FILLING: light and fuel both occupy a chamber until it is full.
branches.cn: 充满：光与燃料都占满腔室，直到再装不下。

branches.en: NO ROOM LEFT: grief and information both leave nothing for anything else.
branches.cn: 再无余地：悲伤与信息都不给别的事物留位置。

intro.en: Flooding is a transparent English derivative of flood, so its morphology is suffixal and Germanic.
intro.cn: flooding 是 flood 的透明英语派生词，其形态构成为日耳曼语后缀法。

definition_zh: v. （烹饪）把油脂或肉汁浇淋在烤肉上；（缝纫）用长针脚粗缝、假缝；（旧用）痛打
definition_en: to moisten roasting meat with fat or its own juices; to join cloth with long loose temporary stitches; in older use, to thrash
core_image: 烤箱门一开，一勺滚热的盘底汁水浇回焦黄的肉面
scene: 烤箱门一开，她就把盘底的汁水浇回肉上。 She opened the oven and used the pan juices to baste the meat.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：baste 指烹饪中把油脂或汁液浇淋在烤肉上；句意是她用盘底肉汁浇淋烤肉。

senses.title: To moisten roasting meat
senses.definition: to pour fat or pan juices over meat while it cooks so that it stays moist
senses.definitionCN: 肉在烤制过程中把油脂或盘底汁液浇在其上，使其不干
senses.example: Baste the joint twice while it rests in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 肉块在炉中静置时浇两次汁。
senses.why: The kitchen sense is the newest of the three, and it is the one most readers meet first.
senses.whyCN: 厨房义是三个义项中最新的一个，也是多数读者最先遇到的。

senses.title: To sew loosely
senses.definition: to join pieces of cloth with long temporary stitches that will be removed later
senses.definitionCN: 用日后会拆掉的长针脚把布料临时缝合
senses.example: She basted the lining before machining the seam.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把衬里粗缝固定，再上机缝接缝。
senses.why: This sense comes from Old French bastir, to build or to sew loosely, so the idea is holding a shape in place.
senses.whyCN: 此义源自古法语 bastir「搭建、松缝」，核心是先把形状固定住。

senses.title: To thrash
senses.definition: in older writing, to beat someone hard
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文献中指狠打某人
senses.example: The old play has a servant basted for his insolence.
senses.exampleCN: 那出旧戏里有个仆人因无礼而被痛打。
senses.why: This verb is probably from Old Norse beysta, to beat, and it survives mainly in older texts.
senses.whyCN: 该动词可能源自古诺斯语 beysta「击打」，如今主要见于旧文献。

intro.en: Baste is really three verbs sharing one spelling: a sewing word from French, a beating word from Norse, and a kitchen word of uncertain origin that won out.
intro.cn: baste 其实是共用一个拼写的三个动词：来自法语的缝纫词、来自诺斯语的击打词，以及来源不明却最终胜出的厨房词。

items.en: Old Norse beysta meant to beat or thump, one possible source of the word.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 beysta 意为击打，是该词的一个可能来源。

items.en: Old French bastir meant to build or to sew loosely, giving the tailoring sense.
items.cn: 古法语 bastir 意为搭建或松缝，给出缝纫那一义。

items.en: Middle English uses the word for long temporary stitches holding cloth in place.
items.cn: 中古英语用该词指把布料临时固定的长针脚。

items.en: A verb meaning to thrash appears in writing, close in sound to the sewing word.
items.cn: 书面语中出现「痛打」义的动词，与缝纫词读音相近。

items.en: Cookery books use the word for moistening roasting meat with fat and juices.
items.cn: 烹饪书用该词指以油脂与肉汁浇淋烤肉。

items.en: The kitchen sense becomes the commonest, and a baster is sold as a tool for it.
items.cn: 厨房义成为最常用义，并出现名为 baster 的专用工具。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the same long vowel and the -aste shape; the near-meaning group splits into kitchen verbs and the tailoring verb, matching the two live senses.
note.cn: 形近组保留同一个长元音与 -aste 字形；近义组分为厨房动词与缝纫动词两支，正对应两个活跃义项。

entries.definition: The bottom or foundation of something.
entries.definitionCN: 底部；基础。

entries.definition: Fibre from the inner bark of trees.
entries.definitionCN: 取自树内皮的纤维。

entries.definition: A thick soft wet mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 稠厚的软糊状物。

entries.definition: Hurried speed of movement.
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙；急速。

entries.definition: To make something a little wet.
entries.definitionCN: 使略湿。

entries.definition: To sew with long loose stitches.
entries.definitionCN: 用长而松的针脚缝。

entries.definition: To coat food to give it a shine.
entries.definitionCN: 给食物涂上一层使其发亮。

entries.definition: To soak food in seasoned liquid before cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 烹调前把食物浸在调味液中。

normalIntro.en: One spelling, three jobs: wet the roast, hold the cloth, or beat the servant. Picture the spoon, the needle and the stick.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拼写，三份工作：浇湿烤肉、固定布料、痛打仆人。分别想象那把勺、那根针和那根棍。

normal.en: A spoon lifting hot juice back onto the meat.
normal.cn: 一把勺把滚热的肉汁浇回肉上。

normal.en: A needle taking long stitches that will come out.
normal.cn: 一根针缝出日后要拆掉的长针脚。

normal.en: Basted is the form you meet in recipes.
normal.cn: basted 是食谱里常见的形式。

normal.en: A baster is the little suction tool for the job.
normal.cn: baster 就是干这活的小吸油管。

normal.en: Baste rhymes with paste, and both are soft and wet.
normal.cn: baste 与 paste 押韵，两者都软而湿。

abstract.en: Care applied in small repeated doses.
abstract.cn: 以小而反复的剂量施加的照料。

abstract.en: A temporary hold that trusts a later seam.
abstract.cn: 一种信赖日后正式缝合的临时固定。

abstract.en: Keeping something from drying out while it changes.
abstract.cn: 在某物变化的过程中不让它干掉。

examples.en: Baste the chicken every half hour.
examples.cn: 每半小时给鸡浇一次汁。

examples.en: The tailor basted the sleeves in by hand.
examples.cn: 裁缝用手针把袖子粗缝上去。

examples.en: A basted roast keeps its colour better.
examples.cn: 浇过汁的烤肉色泽保持得更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「贝斯特」——记一把勺：烤肉时把汁浇回去就是 baste。再记一根针：缝纫的「粗缝」也叫 baste。三义一线：浇汁、假缝、（旧）痛打。

root: 一个拼写三条来源：缝纫义来自古法语 bastir「搭建、松缝」；痛打义可能来自古诺斯语 beysta「击打」；烹饪义 17 世纪见于烹饪书，来源未定，后成为最常用义并催生工具名 baster。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses that happen to share a spelling. Learn them as spoon, needle and stick, in that order of usefulness.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项恰好共用一个拼写。按「勺、针、棍」来记，顺序也正是实用程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spoon of hot pan juice poured back over a browning joint
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺滚热盘汁浇回正在上色的肉块

branches.en: An oven door opened on a rush of steam.
branches.cn: 烤箱门开，热气涌出。

branches.en: A brush drawn across crisp skin.
branches.cn: 刷子在脆皮上抹过。

branches.en: Long white stitches down a lining.
branches.cn: 衬里上一行长长的白针脚。

branches.en: A servant in an old comedy.
branches.cn: 旧喜剧里的一个仆人。

branches.en: Holding moisture or shape until the end.
branches.cn: 把水分或形状保持到最后。

intro.en: Baste is a bare verb root; the endings below build its forms, its tool noun and the wider vocabulary of moistening.
intro.cn: baste 是一个赤裸的动词词根；下面这些词缀构成它的各种形式、工具名词，以及「润湿」这一语义场的更大词汇。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin bastire lies behind the French sewing verb; mare, sea, gives the brine idea in marinate, and humectare means to moisten.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 bastire 是法语缝纫动词的来源；mare「海」给出 marinate 中的「盐水」构想；humectare 意为润湿。

definition_zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的；僵化的；固化的
definition_en: preserved in the form of a fossil, or, figuratively, fixed so long in one form that it can no longer change
core_image: 一片叶子落进湖底，矿物一点点填满它的细胞，千万年后只剩石头上的一道叶脉
scene: 博物馆库房的抽屉里，一片叶子的轮廓被压进灰色石板，叶脉清晰，却已没有一丝有机物残留。 The fossilized leaf in the drawer keeps every vein although nothing organic survives.
sceneCN: 这里 fossilized 指「有机体被矿物质替换、以化石形态保存下来」（第 1 个义项：生物遗体或遗迹经矿化作用定形）；句意为抽屉里的这片叶子虽保留了全部叶脉，有机物却已完全被矿物取代。可辨识物件：石板、叶脉纹、抽屉、标本签、软毛刷。

pos.zh: 化成化石的；以化石形态保存的
僵化的；固化的；停滞不前的（比喻）
（fossilize 的过去式与过去分词）使化石化；使僵化

senses.title: Turned to stone by mineral replacement
senses.titleCN: 矿化成石：有机质被矿物替换
senses.definition: preserved as a fossil because minerals have slowly replaced the original organic material
senses.definitionCN: 因矿物缓慢替换原有有机质而以化石形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized wood still shows the grain of the original trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这块石化木仍能看出原树干的纹理。
senses.why: Fossil comes from Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig; the -ized ending says the thing has undergone that change and is now stone-like.
senses.whyCN: fossil 出自拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」；-ized 结尾表示该物已经历这一变化，如今状如石头。

senses.title: Preserved as a trace fossil
senses.definition: kept as a footprint, burrow, egg or other trace rather than as the body itself
senses.definitionCN: 以脚印、洞穴、蛋等遗迹而非遗体本身的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized footprints record a walk across wet ash.
senses.exampleCN: 这些化石脚印记录了一次走过湿灰地的行走。
senses.why: A trace is also fossilized when the sediment hardens around the impression; the body is gone but the shape it made has become stone.
senses.whyCN: 当沉积物在印痕周围硬化时，遗迹同样被化石化；身体不在了，它留下的形状却成了石头。

senses.title: Fixed in an outdated form
senses.titleCN: 僵化：制度或观念不再变化
senses.definition: of an institution, idea or practice, fixed so long in one shape that reform becomes impossible
senses.definitionCN: 指制度、观念或做法长期固定于一种形态，以致无法改革
senses.example: The committee had fossilized into a ritual of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这个委员会已经僵化成一道审批仪式。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the geological process: what should have decayed instead hardened, and hardening removes the ability to adapt.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了地质过程：本该腐朽的东西反而硬化了，而硬化剥夺了适应能力。

senses.title: Stuck in old habits
senses.titleCN: 停滞：人停留在旧习惯里
senses.definition: of a person or group, no longer able to change because habits have hardened
senses.definitionCN: 指人或群体因习惯硬化而不再能改变
senses.example: He had fossilized in his opinions by the age of forty.
senses.exampleCN: 他四十岁时观念就已僵化。
senses.why: The same image applied to a mind: repeated behaviour sets like cement, and the set shape resists new evidence.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象用于心智：重复的行为像水泥一样凝固，凝固的形状抗拒新证据。

senses.title: A form frozen in a language
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, kept in an earlier form inside a fixed expression
senses.definitionCN: 指词或短语在固定表达中以较早的形式保存下来
senses.example: The fossilized phrase still uses a verb form no one speaks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个固化短语仍使用无人再说的动词形式。
senses.why: Languages preserve dead forms inside idioms the way rock preserves shells: the surrounding expression stops the change.
senses.whyCN: 语言在习语中保存已死的形式，就像岩石保存贝壳：周围的表达阻止了变化。

senses.title: Dated and unable to update
senses.titleCN: 定型的：因年代久远而无法更新
senses.definition: of a system or style, preserved in an earlier state and unable to modernise
senses.definitionCN: 指体系或风格停留在较早状态、无法现代化
senses.example: The fossilized software could not read any file made after two thousand five.
senses.exampleCN: 这套固化的软件读不了那一年之后生成的任何文件。
senses.why: Systems also harden: once dependencies set, every later change costs more than the system can pay, so the old shape survives.
senses.whyCN: 系统也会硬化：依赖一旦固定，此后每次改动的代价都超出系统所能支付，旧形状便存活下来。

senses.title: Bone filled with mineral
senses.definition: of bone, shell or tooth, with its pores filled by mineral so that the original shape is kept
senses.definitionCN: 指骨骼、贝壳或牙齿的孔隙被矿物充填，从而保留原形
senses.example: The fossilized tooth is heavy because mineral fills every pore.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗化石牙很重，因为矿物填满了每个孔隙。
senses.why: Hard parts fossilize best because they already contain mineral; groundwater adds more, and the object gains weight and permanence.
senses.whyCN: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为它们本就含矿物；地下水再添矿物，物件便增加重量与持久性。

senses.title: Frozen in a single moment
senses.definition: used figuratively for anything that seems arrested at one moment and never moves on
senses.definitionCN: 比喻任何仿佛停在一刻、再也不向前的事物
senses.example: The village felt fossilized in the decade the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 这座村庄仿佛冻结在矿场关闭的那个年代。
senses.why: The image reaches its limit here: not merely old, but arrested, as if time had stopped and left the object inside a single layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象在此达到极限：不只是旧，而是被定格，仿佛时间停止，把物件封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is the past participle of fossilize, built on fossil plus the suffix -ize. Fossil goes back to Latin fossilis, dug up, from fodere, to dig. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: fossilized 是 fossilize 的过去分词，由 fossil 加后缀 -ize 构成。fossil 上溯拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」，源于 fodere「挖掘」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fodere meant to dig; its participle fossus, dug, produced fossilis, a thing dug out of the earth.
items.cn: fodere 意为挖掘；其分词 fossus「被挖的」产生 fossilis，即从地里挖出之物。

items.en: Fossilis named anything obtained by digging, including stones and buried remains; English adopted it in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: fossilis 指任何挖掘所得之物，包括石头与埋藏的遗存；英语在十七世纪引入这个词。

items.en: As geology took shape, fossil narrowed to the preserved traces of organisms, and fossilize was coined for the process that produces them.
items.cn: 随着地质学成形，fossil 收窄为生物遗存的保存形态，fossilize 则为产生这一形态的过程而造。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the participle was already used of institutions and opinions that had hardened beyond change.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，这一分词已用于形容硬化到无法改变的制度与观念。

items.en: Source uncertain: no single author is credited with coining fossilize, and the date of its first geological use is not fixed; the suffix -ize was freely added to nouns in that period.
items.cn: 来源不确定：没有辞书把 fossilize 的创造归给某一位作者，其首次地质学用法也无定年；当时 -ize 后缀可自由加在名词上。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same fossil stock; the second group holds words for things that have stopped changing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 fossil 词干的词；第二组是表示「不再变化」的词。

entries.definition: The preserved remains itself; fossilized describes the state the remains reached.
entries.definitionCN: 指保存下来的遗存本身；fossilized 描述它达到的状态。

entries.definition: The process verb, to turn into a fossil or to become rigid; the participle names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 过程动词，指变成化石或变得僵硬；分词形式指结果。

entries.definition: From the same fodere, to dig, but it describes animals adapted for digging, not preserved remains.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 fodere「挖掘」，但形容适应掘土的动物，而非保存下来的遗存。

entries.definition: Literally turned to stone by mineral replacement; it is the closest physical synonym, while fossilized can also mean trace-preserved.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指被矿物替换成石头；它是最接近的物理同义词，而 fossilized 也可指遗迹保存。

entries.definition: Stiff and unwilling to bend; it describes the behaviour, while fossilized adds the image of geological hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 僵硬、不愿弯曲；它描述行为，而 fossilized 增加了地质硬化的意象。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned and out of use; it says nothing about hardening, only about surviving past its time.
entries.definitionCN: 古旧而不再使用；它不涉及硬化，只说明活过了它的时代。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the digging root, the -ize suffix, the trace fossils, and the metaphor of hardening.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示挖掘的词根、-ize 后缀、遗迹化石，以及硬化的比喻。

normal.en: fodere, to dig, gives fossilis, dug up: a fossil is literally something dug out of the ground.
normal.cn: fodere「挖掘」派生 fossilis「被挖出的」：化石字面就是从地里挖出的东西。

normal.en: -ize turns the noun into a process, and -ed marks the result: the thing has been through the process.
normal.cn: -ize 把名词变成过程，-ed 标记结果：该物已经历这一过程。

normal.en: Body fossils keep the organism; trace fossils keep what it did, such as footprints and burrows.
normal.cn: 实体化石保存生物本身；遗迹化石保存它做过的事，如脚印与洞穴。

normal.en: Hard parts fossilize best because bone and shell already contain mineral.
normal.cn: 硬质部分最易化石化，因为骨与壳本就含矿物。

normal.en: Applied to people, the same word accuses them of having hardened instead of growing.
normal.cn: 用于人时，同一个词是在指责他们硬化了，而不是成长了。

abstract.en: Abstractly, fossilization is change that stops: the object keeps its shape by losing its capacity to respond.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，化石化是停止的变化：物件靠失去回应能力来保住形状。

abstract.en: Preservation and death are the same process seen from two sides: what survives is what could not decay.
abstract.cn: 保存与死亡是同一过程的两面：活下来的，正是无法腐朽的部分。

abstract.en: Every institution should ask whether its stability is growth or fossilization.
abstract.cn: 每个机构都该问：它的稳定是成长，还是僵化。

examples.en: The fossilized reef shows that a warm sea once covered this desert.
examples.cn: 这片石化礁石说明温暖的海曾覆盖过这片沙漠。

examples.en: Fossilized pollen in the sediment records the plants of that era.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的化石花粉记录了那个时代的植物。

examples.en: The department had fossilized around a procedure no one could defend.
examples.cn: 这个部门围绕一道无人能辩护的程序僵化了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fossil（化石）+ ized（已经变成）」——已经变成化石的 → 化石化的、僵化的

root: 拉丁 fossilis「被挖出的」（源于 fodere「挖掘」）+ 动词后缀 -ize 的过去分词 -ized；字面为「已被挖出、已成化石的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hardening: organic matter becomes stone, a trace becomes stone, and then institutions, minds, phrases, systems and whole places become unable to change.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次硬化展开：有机物变成石头，遗迹变成石头，随后制度、心智、短语、系统乃至整个地方都变得无法改变。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft tissue replaced grain by grain until only a stone copy remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：柔软组织被一粒粒矿物替换，最后只剩一份石质副本。

branches.en: THE BODY IN STONE: replacement and pore-filling are two routes to the same heavy copy.
branches.cn: 石中的身体：替换与充填是通往同一份沉重副本的两条路。

branches.en: THE SHAPE LEFT BEHIND: a footprint hardens into evidence even when no body is there.
branches.cn: 留下的形状：即使没有身体，脚印也会硬化成证据。

branches.en: HARDENED INSTITUTIONS AND MINDS: what should have adapted instead set like cement.
branches.cn: 硬化的制度与心智：本该适应的东西却像水泥一样凝固。

branches.en: THE IDIOM AS AMBER: a fixed phrase preserves a dead form exactly as resin preserves an insect.
branches.cn: 习语如琥珀：固定短语保存已死的形式，正如树脂保存昆虫。

branches.en: ARRESTED TIME: systems and places stop updating and seem sealed inside one layer.
branches.cn: 被定格的时间：系统与地方停止更新，仿佛被封在某一层里。

intro.en: Fossilized is transparent: a Latin-derived noun, a productive verb suffix and a past-participle ending.
intro.cn: fossilized 的构造很透明：一个拉丁来源的名词、一个能产动词后缀与一个过去分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin fodere, to dig, gives fossilis and then fossil; English adds -ize and -ed. The same fodere also gives fossorial, describing digging animals.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fodere「挖掘」衍生 fossilis，再进入英语为 fossil；英语加上 -ize 与 -ed。同一 fodere 还衍生 fossorial，形容掘土动物。

items.example: Fodere is the source of fossil and fossorial.
items.exampleCN: fodere 是 fossil 与 fossorial 的来源。

items.example: Fossilis described stones taken from deep ground.
items.exampleCN: fossilis 形容从深土中取出的石头。

items.example: The fossil was found in marine limestone.
items.exampleCN: 这块化石发现于海相石灰岩中。

items.example: Fossil plus -ize means to become a fossil.
items.exampleCN: fossil 加 -ize 意为变成化石。

items.meaning: to turn into a fossil, or to become rigid
items.example: Wood can fossilize in mineral-rich water.
items.exampleCN: 木材在富含矿物质的水中可以化石化。

items.example: The -ed ending marks the completed process.
items.exampleCN: -ed 词尾标记已完成的过程。

items.meaning: the process of becoming a fossil
items.example: Fossilization needs rapid burial and mineral water.
items.exampleCN: 化石化需要迅速埋藏与含矿物质的水。

items.example: The fossiliferous layer is dark and hard.
items.exampleCN: 含化石的层位颜色深、质地硬。

items.example: Fossorial mammals have strong forelimbs.
items.exampleCN: 掘土哺乳动物前肢强壮。

items.example: The fosse around the fort is still visible.
items.exampleCN: 堡垒周围的壕沟仍可见。

definition_zh: 珊瑚礁（由珊瑚骨骼堆积而成、接近海面的礁体及其生态系统）
definition_en: a ridge or platform near the sea surface built mainly by coral, together with the community that lives on it
core_image: 清透的浅海上，一道浅色的脊把深蓝与碧绿分开，脊上布满枝状与块状的珊瑚
scene: 小船驶进清透的浅海，船底突然出现一道浅色的脊，把深蓝的水与碧绿的水分开。 A coral reef lay just beneath the hull, its top within reach of the sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 coral reef 指「接近海面、由珊瑚建造的礁体」（第 1 个义项：珊瑚骨骼堆成的浅海礁脊）；句意为船底正下方就是一道顶部能被阳光照到的珊瑚礁。

derivatives.zh: 礁坪（礁体顶部的浅平区）

senses.title: A ridge built by coral near the surface
senses.definition: a stony ridge or platform in shallow tropical water, raised by the accumulated skeletons of coral
senses.definitionCN: 在浅热带海域由珊瑚骨骼堆积抬升而成的石质脊或平台
senses.example: A coral reef lay just beneath the hull.
senses.exampleCN: 船底正下方就是一道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: Coral supplies the builder and reef supplies the shape, so the compound names a structure defined by what made it.
senses.whyCN: coral 提供建造者，reef 提供形状，因此这个复合词按「由什么造成」来定义一种结构。

senses.title: The community living on the structure
senses.definition: the dense community of fish, invertebrates and algae that depends on the reef framework
senses.definitionCN: 依赖礁体结构生存的鱼类、无脊椎动物与藻类群落
senses.example: The coral reef supports more species than the open sea around it.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁支撑的物种比周围开阔海更多。
senses.why: Ecology names the habitat by its frame, so the phrase shifts from stone to the life that occupies it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学以框架来命名栖息地，于是这个短语从石头转向占据它的生命。

senses.title: A charted hazard to navigation
senses.titleCN: 海图上标出的航行障碍
senses.definition: a shallow reef marked on charts because it can damage a hull
senses.definitionCN: 在海图上标出、可能损伤船体的浅礁
senses.example: The chart marks the coral reef two miles offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 海图在离岸两英里处标出了这道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: For sailors the reef is first of all an obstruction, so the phrase enters navigation language as a warning.
senses.whyCN: 对水手来说礁首先是障碍，因此这个短语以警告的身份进入航海语言。

senses.title: An ancient reef now in rock
senses.titleCN: 如今留在岩层中的古礁
senses.definition: the fossilized structure of a former coral reef, often preserved as limestone
senses.definitionCN: 旧日珊瑚礁被石化后的结构，常以石灰岩形式保存
senses.example: An ancient coral reef now stands inland as a low ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一道古代珊瑚礁如今作为低矮的山脊立在内陆。
senses.why: Geology reads the same structure in stone, so the phrase survives the death of the entire community.
senses.whyCN: 地质学在石头里读出同一结构，因此这个短语在整片群落死亡之后仍然存在。

senses.title: A resource for tourism and fishing
senses.definition: a reef valued as a dive site or fishing ground that brings income
senses.definitionCN: 作为潜水点或渔场而带来收入的礁
senses.example: Divers travel thousands of miles to see that coral reef.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水者远行千里只为看那道珊瑚礁。
senses.why: The phrase turns into an economic asset once people pay to visit or harvest from it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们付费到访或从中捕捞，这个短语就变成经济资产。

senses.title: A unit of conservation
senses.definition: a reef managed as a protected area, with rules on fishing and anchoring
senses.definitionCN: 作为保护区管理、对捕捞与抛锚设有规定的礁
senses.example: The marine park covers three coral reefs and their lagoons.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋公园涵盖三道珊瑚礁及其潟湖。
senses.why: Conservation needs countable units, and a whole reef becomes one manageable object.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作需要有可数的单元，一整道礁于是成为一个可管理的对象。

senses.title: A type in the fringing-barrier-atoll series
senses.titleCN: 裙礁—堡礁—环礁序列中的类型
senses.definition: one of the standard forms of reef, classed by its relation to a coast or lagoon
senses.definitionCN: 按与海岸或潟湖的关系划分的标准礁型之一
senses.example: A barrier coral reef rings the island at some distance from the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 一道堡礁在离岸较远处环抱这座岛。
senses.why: Darwin's classification turned reefs into types, and the compound is used with fringing, barrier and atoll.
senses.whyCN: 达尔文的分类把礁分成类型，这个复合词常与 fringing、barrier、atoll 搭配使用。

senses.title: A dense, sheltering structure, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：密集而能藏身的结构
senses.definition: a crowded, branching structure that offers many niches and hiding places, compared to a reef
senses.definitionCN: 像珊瑚礁那样密集分枝、提供许多小生境与藏身处的结构
senses.example: The old market was a coral reef of stalls where a stranger could disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 旧市场像一片珊瑚礁，摊位密集，陌生人一进去就不见了。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps the reef's two features, dense growth and many hiding places, and drops the water.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义保留礁的两个特征——密集生长与众多藏身处，只去掉海水。

intro.en: Coral reef joins a Greek-derived noun of uncertain origin to an Old Norse word for a sea ridge; the compound is modern, the parts are old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coral reef 把一个来源不确定的希腊系名词与一个古诺斯语「海脊」词连在一起；复合词是近代的，两部分都很古老。年代均为约数。

items.en: Coral comes from Greek korallion, the red coral of the Mediterranean. The Greek word's deeper origin is not established; a Semitic loan is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.cn: coral 来自希腊 korallion，指地中海红珊瑚。这个希腊词的更深来源没有定论；源自闪米特语只是一种假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin corallium and Old French coral carried the word to English, first as the precious red material rather than as a reef-building animal.
items.cn: 拉丁 corallium 与古法语 coral 把这个词带到英语，最初指贵重的红色材料，而非造礁动物。

items.en: Reef comes from Old Norse rif, 'ridge at sea', the same shape-word used for a rib; whether the sea sense grew from 'rib' or from a 'tearing' verb is debated.
items.cn: reef 来自古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」，与表示「肋骨」的是同一个形状词；海义究竟由「肋骨」还是由某个「撕裂」动词发展而来，仍有争论。

items.en: Coral reef is recorded from the eighteenth century, when Pacific and Indian Ocean voyagers began charting shallow coral structures.
items.cn: coral reef 自 18 世纪有记录，当时太平洋与印度洋的航海者开始测绘浅水珊瑚结构。

items.en: Darwin's 1842 book on coral reefs fixed the familiar series fringing reef, barrier reef and atoll, and the compound entered general science with it.
items.cn: 达尔文 1842 年关于珊瑚礁的著作确立了裙礁、堡礁、环礁这一熟悉序列，这个复合词也随之进入通用科学语。

items.en: Source uncertain (both parts): korallion has no agreed etymology, and the relation of rif to 'rib' and to 'tear' remains unsettled; exact first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（两部分皆是）：korallion 没有公认词源，rif 与「肋骨」「撕裂」的关系亦无定论；确切首见年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and near-spellings of the phrase itself; group two holds other shallow-water structures that are often confused with a coral reef.
note.cn: 第一组是这个短语自身的组成部分与形近词；第二组是常与珊瑚礁混淆的其他浅水结构。

entries.definition: The animal and its skeleton; a coral reef is the structure, so the two words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物及其骨骼；珊瑚礁是整体结构，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Any ridge near the surface, of rock, sand or coral; without coral it may still be a reef but not a coral reef.
entries.definitionCN: 任何接近水面的岩、沙或珊瑚脊；没有珊瑚时仍可称礁，但不能称珊瑚礁。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of or like coral; it also names red algae that cement reefs but are not coral.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为珊瑚的或似珊瑚的；也指胶结礁体的红藻，但那些藻不是珊瑚。

entries.definition: An island built of coral debris and sand; it may sit on a reef, but the phrase names dry land rather than the submerged structure.
entries.definitionCN: 由珊瑚碎屑与沙堆成的岛；它可能坐落在礁上，但这个短语指陆地，而非水下结构。

entries.definition: A coral reef forming a ring around a lagoon; an atoll is one type of coral reef, not a synonym for all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 环绕潟湖成环的珊瑚礁；环礁是珊瑚礁的一种类型，并非所有珊瑚礁的同义词。

entries.definition: A reef running parallel to a coast with a lagoon between; it is a coral reef in a particular position.
entries.definitionCN: 与海岸平行、中间隔有潟湖的礁；它是处在特定位置的珊瑚礁。

entries.definition: A shallow bank of sand or rock that hazards ships; it need not be built by coral and need not break the surface.
entries.definitionCN: 危及船只的浅沙洲或浅岩滩；它未必由珊瑚建造，也未必露出水面。

entries.definition: A small low island of sand on a reef; the reef is the structure beneath, the cay is the dry patch above.
entries.definitionCN: 礁上低矮的小沙岛；礁是下面的结构，cay 是上面的干出部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: coral names the builder, reef names the ridge: together they name a structure and its maker.
normal.cn: coral 标建造者，reef 标脊状结构：合起来就是结构与制造者。

normal.en: The plural is coral reefs, with the -s on reef, not on coral.
normal.cn: 复数是 coral reefs，-s 加在 reef 上，不加在 coral 上。

normal.en: Darwin's three types are fringing reef, barrier reef and atoll, all of them coral reefs.
normal.cn: 达尔文的三类是裙礁、堡礁、环礁，三者都是珊瑚礁。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: coral reef ecosystem, coral reef conservation, coral reef bleaching.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：珊瑚礁生态系统、珊瑚礁保护、珊瑚礁白化。

normal.en: A cay is dry sand on a reef; a shoal is shallow but not necessarily coral.
normal.cn: cay 是礁上的干沙；shoal 是浅滩，但未必由珊瑚构成。

abstract.en: Picture a pale line in blue water where waves break before they reach the shore.
abstract.cn: 想象蓝色水面上一条浅色的线，浪在到岸之前先在那里碎开。

abstract.en: Picture a stone city under water, every window filled with a fish.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水下石城，每个窗口里都有一条鱼。

abstract.en: Picture a market so crowded that it hides anyone who walks in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个拥挤到能把走进的人藏起来的市场。

examples.en: The coral reef absorbs wave energy before it reaches the beach.
examples.cn: 珊瑚礁在波浪到达海滩之前吸收其能量。

examples.en: Sediment from the cleared hillside smothered the coral reef below.
examples.cn: 被清空的山坡冲下的泥沙把下面的珊瑚礁埋住了。

examples.en: Scientists survey the coral reef every year to count fish and bleached colonies.
examples.cn: 科学家每年调查这片珊瑚礁，统计鱼类与白化的珊瑚群体。

dict_mnemonic.text: coral（珊瑚）+ reef（礁）——珊瑚搭起来的礁就是珊瑚礁；把两个词连起来记最省力

root: coral（希腊 korallion「红珊瑚」，更深来源不确定）+ reef（古诺斯语 rif「海中的脊」）；两词在英语中合为复合名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the structure itself to what lives on it and what people do with it: ridge, community, hazard, fossil, resource, protected unit, reef type and finally a metaphor for any crowded shelter.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从结构本身移向栖居其上的生命与人的利用：礁脊、群落、航行障碍、化石、资源、保护单元、礁型，最后是任何密集庇护所的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale ridge in clear water, splitting deep blue from turquoise.
core.cn: 核心意象：清透水中的一道浅色脊，把深蓝与碧绿分开。

branches.en: FORM: whatever its type, the object is a ridge raised by coral.
branches.cn: 形态：无论哪一类型，这个对象都是珊瑚抬升出的脊。

branches.en: LIFE: the stone becomes a habitat, and the phrase names the community too.
branches.cn: 生命：石头变成栖息地，短语也指其中的群落。

branches.en: USE AND DANGER: the same ridge is an asset to divers and a hazard to hulls.
branches.cn: 利用与危险：同一道脊对潜水者是资源，对船体是危险。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: the fossil reef keeps the shape after the sea is gone.
branches.cn: 深时：海水退去后，化石礁仍保留形状。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT AND METAPHOR: a countable unit to protect, and a crowded shelter to imagine.
branches.cn: 管理与比喻：既是可保护的单位，也是可想象的密集庇护所。

intro.en: Coral reef is a two-noun compound, so its morphology is compounding rather than prefixation; each half still has its own family.
intro.cn: coral reef 是双名词复合词，其构词方式是复合而非加前缀；两半各自仍有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Only coral has a Latin source, corallium; reef is Germanic, from Old Norse rif, so the compound joins two different language stocks.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 coral 有拉丁来源 corallium；reef 属日耳曼语，来自古诺斯语 rif，因此这个复合词连接了两个不同的语源。

items.structure: Old French coral, from Latin corallium
items.example: Coral supplies the building material.
Reef supplies the shape.

items.meaning: a coral-built ridge near the surface
items.example: The coral reef shelters the bay.
Coral reefs ring the archipelago.

items.structure: coral reef used as a modifier
items.example: Coral-reef fish rarely stray into open water.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁鱼类很少游到开阔水域。

items.meaning: the shallow top surface of a reef
items.example: The reef flat dries at extreme low tide.
items.exampleCN: 极低潮时礁坪会露出水面。

items.meaning: the raised outer edge of a reef
items.example: Waves break hardest on the reef crest.

items.meaning: coral species that raise reef frameworks
items.example: Reef-building coral needs clear warm water.
items.exampleCN: 造礁珊瑚需要清澈温暖的水。

definition_zh: 监督；监管；疏忽；漏看；照管的责任
definition_en: the act of watching over something, or a failure to notice something
core_image: 一只眼越过桌面看向远处，近处的一行字反而没看见
scene: 审计发现付款环节漏了一道复核，随后建议把看管的责任提到更高一层。 The audit found an oversight in the payment process.
sceneCN: 这里 oversight 指因疏忽而漏看的一处（第 2 个义项：无意的遗漏）；句意：审计发现付款流程中有一处漏看。图中可辨识物件：审计报告、付款单、复核签栏、红色标记。

pos.zh: 监督；监管；疏忽；漏看；照管责任

senses.title: The act of watching over work
senses.definition: the act of watching over work or people and being responsible for them
senses.definitionCN: 看住工作或人员并为之负责的行为
senses.example: Oversight of the laboratory was given to a new committee.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的监督权交给了一个新委员会。
senses.why: Over and sight make the word a plain English picture of an eye kept above something.
senses.whyCN: 「在上」与「看见」两个构件让这个词成为一幅直白的图画：一只眼留在某物上方。

senses.title: An accidental omission
senses.definition: a failure to notice or do something that should have been noticed or done
senses.definitionCN: 该注意到或该做的事没有被注意到或做到
senses.example: By an oversight, her name was left off the list.
senses.exampleCN: 由于疏忽，她的名字被漏在名单之外。
senses.why: If the eye is fixed on the far view, the near line escapes it; that is how watching turns into missing.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛盯着远处时，近处那一行就逃过去了；看管正是这样变成漏看。

senses.title: Official supervision by a body
senses.titleCN: 机构对某领域的正式监管
senses.definition: the supervision exercised by a public body over an industry or service
senses.definitionCN: 公共机构对某个行业或服务施加的监督
senses.example: Banking oversight moved to a single agency.
senses.exampleCN: 银行业监管移交给了单一机构。
senses.why: When the eye belongs to a public body, the word names an institution rather than a glance.
senses.whyCN: 当这只眼属于公共机构，这个词命名的就是一个机构，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: A careless mistake
senses.definition: a mistake made because something was not checked
senses.definitionCN: 因某项事情未被核查而产生的错误
senses.example: Two oversights in the invoice cost the firm a week.
senses.exampleCN: 发票上的两处疏漏让公司损失了一周时间。
senses.why: The omission is the missing look; the mistake is what the missing look let through.
senses.whyCN: 疏漏是少看了那一眼；错误是少看那一眼放进来的东西。

senses.title: The duty of watching
senses.definition: the responsibility for checking that something is done properly
senses.definitionCN: 核查某事是否被妥善完成的职责
senses.example: The safety of the archive is under his oversight.
senses.exampleCN: 档案的安全由他负责照管。
senses.why: Here the word is not the act or the failure but the charge laid on a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词既不是动作也不是失误，而是压在某人身上的职责。

senses.title: Legislative supervision of government
senses.titleCN: 立法机关对政府的监督
senses.definition: the checking of a government's actions by a legislature or a court
senses.definitionCN: 立法机关或法院对政府行为的核查
senses.example: Congressional oversight delayed the appointment for months.
senses.exampleCN: 国会监督让这项任命拖了几个月。
senses.why: The eye of one branch is deliberately placed above another, so oversight becomes a constitutional device.
senses.whyCN: 一支机构的眼被有意放在另一支上方，监督于是成了宪制设计。

senses.title: Guardianship of a dependent person
senses.definition: the watching care given to someone who cannot look after themselves
senses.definitionCN: 对无法自理者给予的看护
senses.example: The child remained under her aunt's oversight.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子仍由姑母照管。
senses.why: The same word can mean protective care when the watched person cannot answer back.
senses.whyCN: 当被看者无法回应时，同一个词可以指保护性的照料。

senses.title: The state of being checked
senses.definition: the condition of having one's work or conduct checked by another
senses.definitionCN: 工作或行为受到他人核查的状态
senses.example: Every transfer now takes place under independent oversight.
senses.exampleCN: 现在每笔划转都在独立监督之下进行。
senses.why: The noun can stand on the watched side as well, naming the situation rather than the watcher.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能站在被看的那一边，命名情形而不是看的人。

intro.en: Oversight joins over and sight, both native English words. It first meant supervision, and later, by the logic of looking past a thing, also came to mean a failure to notice.
intro.cn: oversight 由 over 与 sight 两个英语本族词接成。它最初指监督，后来顺着「目光越过某物」的逻辑，也指漏看。

items.en: Ofer 'over, above' gives the first half and keeps the picture of a gaze from a higher place.
items.cn: ofer「在上、越过」给出前半，并保留目光来自高处的画面。

items.en: The noun sihth 'a seeing' became sight, and it supplies the second half of the compound.
items.cn: 名词 sihth「看见」演变为 sight，提供这个复合词的后半。

items.en: Over and sight were joined to name the act of looking over something, at first with no hint of failure.
items.cn: over 与 sight 合成一体，命名「从上方看某物」的行为，最初毫无失误之意。

items.en: The sense of a missed detail is generally dated to the seventeenth century, when looking over a thing could also mean looking past it.
items.cn: 「漏掉的细节」这一义一般被定在十七世纪，当时「看过某物」也能表示「目光越过它」。

items.en: Legislatures and regulators made oversight a standing arrangement in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.
items.cn: 立法机关与监管机构在十八、十九世纪把监督变成常设安排。

items.en: The first dates for the noun and for its negative sense are approximate; the order of the two senses is reliable.
items.cn: 这个名词及其否定义的最早年代都是约数；两义的先后顺序可靠。

note.en: The first group shares the over or sight pieces; the second group names neighbouring systems of checking and missing.
note.cn: 第一组共享 over 或 sight 构件；第二组是相邻的核查与遗漏说法。

entries.definition: The verb, which never means to miss something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，从不表示漏看。

entries.definition: The person who holds the watching role.
entries.definitionCN: 担任看管角色的人。

entries.definition: The noun of seeing that supplies the second half of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「看见」的名词，提供这个词的后半。

entries.definition: Also built from over, and it carries both the viewing and the missing sense, much as oversight does.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由表示「在上」的构件构成，也兼有俯瞰与漏看两义，与 oversight 颇为平行。

entries.definition: The Latin-derived word for the same watching, usually without the negative sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同义的拉丁来源词，通常不含否定义。

entries.definition: Close, often covert watching of a person or place.
entries.definitionCN: 对人或者地方进行密切、常为隐蔽的观察。

entries.definition: The rules imposed by an authority rather than the watching itself.
entries.definitionCN: 主管机关施加的规则，而不是看管本身。

entries.definition: The act of leaving something out, which is exactly what an oversight is.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物遗漏掉的行为，正是 oversight 所指。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real English pieces and the real institutional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实的英语构件与真实的制度用语。

normal.en: Over plus sight is the whole picture: a gaze from above.
normal.cn: 「在上」加「看见」就是整幅画面：从上而下的目光。

normal.en: The family runs oversee, overseer, oversight and overseen.
normal.cn: 同族词有 oversee、overseer、oversaw 与 overseen。

normal.en: Institutional phrases mark it: congressional oversight, regulatory oversight, oversight board.
normal.cn: 制度用语标出它的用法：国会监督、监管、监督委员会。

normal.en: The negative sense comes from looking past a thing rather than at it.
normal.cn: 否定义来自目光越过某物，而不是落在它上面。

normal.en: Overlook shows the same double life, which helps explain why oversight carries both meanings.
normal.cn: overlook 也有同样的两面，这有助于解释 oversight 为何兼有褒贬。

abstract.en: Picture a watchman scanning the horizon while a gate stands open behind him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名看守扫视远方，身后的门却敞着。

abstract.en: Picture a signature line that nobody read because everyone trusted the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一行签字谁也没读，因为人人都信那张纸。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that checks the far corner and forgets the one under the lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手去查远处的角落，却忘了灯下那一个。

examples.en: Oversight of the project passed to a committee of five.
examples.cn: 项目的监督移交给了五人委员会。

examples.en: A single oversight in the labelling kept the shipment at the border.
examples.cn: 标签上的一处疏漏让这批货卡在边境。

examples.en: The agency was created to provide independent oversight.
examples.cn: 设立这个机构是为了提供独立监督。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「over（在上）+ sight（看）」——在上面看是监督，看漏了就是疏忽

root: 英语本族复合词：表示「在上」的构件 + 表示「看见」的构件；先指监督，十七世纪起引申出「漏看、疏忽」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses hold both halves of the word: the act of watching, an accidental omission, official regulation, the mistake that follows, the duty of watching, legislative checking, care of a dependent and the state of being checked.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项握住这个词的两面：看管这个动作、无意的遗漏、正式监管、随之而来的错误、看管的职责、立法监督、对受抚养者的照管，以及被核查的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze fixed on the horizon while the line under the lamp goes unread.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光盯着远方，灯下那一行却没被读到。

branches.en: ACT AND DUTY: watching something, and being charged with watching it.
branches.cn: 动作与职责：看住某物，以及被交付看住它的责任。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a public body, and a legislature placed above a government.
branches.cn: 制度：一个公共机构，以及被置于政府之上的立法机关。

branches.en: THE MISSED LINE: first the omission, then the error it lets through.
branches.cn: 漏掉的一行：先是遗漏，再是它放进来的错误。

branches.en: PROTECTIVE CARE: when the watched person cannot answer back, watching becomes guardianship.
branches.cn: 保护性照料：当被看者无法回应，看管就变成监护。

branches.en: THE WATCHED SIDE: the same noun names the state of being checked.
branches.cn: 被看的一面：同一个名词也命名被核查的状态。

intro.en: Oversight is a native English compound, so it has no Latin ancestors; its two pieces come from Old English and still work separately.
intro.cn: oversight 是英语本族复合词，因此没有拉丁祖先；两个构件来自古英语，至今仍能独立使用。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are over and sight, and both remain common English words; no Latin source is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件是 over 与 sight，两者至今都是常用英语词；不涉及拉丁来源。

items.example: The prefix keeps the gaze at a height.
items.exampleCN: 前缀让目光保持在高度上。

items.structure: Old English noun, from the verb to see
items.meaning: the act or power of seeing
items.example: The second half is the eye itself.
The compound holds both a virtue and a failure.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词同时含着美德与失误。

items.example: The verb is the working half of the pair.
items.exampleCN: 动词是这一对里干活的那一半。

items.example: The person who holds the eye.
The phrase fixes the institutional sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语固定了制度义。

items.example: The fixed phrase marks the negative sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个固定说法标出否定义。

items.meaning: a session that checks a government
items.example: The phrase belongs to legislative practice.

definition_zh: 反气旋；高气压系统
definition_en: a weather system with high pressure at its center, where winds spiral outward and skies stay calm
core_image: 一锅缓慢向外旋开的漩涡，中心晴朗无云
scene: 连日的雨停了，预报图上一个巨大的圆盘正缓缓盖上这座城市。 A summer anticyclone brought a week of clear, windless skies.
sceneCN: 这里 anticyclone 是「反气旋」（第 1 个义项：中心高压、气流向外的天气系统）；句意为夏季反气旋带来一周晴朗无风的天气。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「反气旋的」
同族基础词，义为「气旋；低压系统」

senses.title: A high-pressure weather system
senses.definition: an area of high atmospheric pressure around which winds circulate outward, bringing settled weather
senses.definitionCN: 高气压区，风绕其中心向外旋转，带来稳定天气
senses.example: Fog formed overnight under the anticyclone.
senses.exampleCN: 反气旋控制下，夜间起了雾。
senses.why: The winds run opposite to a cyclone, so the prefix anti- 'against' was attached to cyclone 'wheel'.
senses.whyCN: 风向与气旋相反，所以在 cyclone「轮转」前加上 anti-「反向」前缀。

senses.title: Opposing a cyclone in direction of spin
senses.definition: describing winds or rotation running opposite to the direction of a cyclone in the same hemisphere
senses.definitionCN: 描述在同一半球内与气旋旋转方向相反的风或环流
senses.example: The ocean eddy shows anticyclonic rotation, the reverse of the storm's spin.
senses.exampleCN: 这个海洋涡旋呈反气旋式旋转，与风暴的转向相反。
senses.why: The same anti- 'opposite' applies not to weather quality but to the wheel's direction itself.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 anti-「反向」在此不指天气性质，而指风轮本身的转向。

intro.en: Anticyclone is anti- 'against' plus cyclone, from Greek kyklon, a noun from kyklos 'wheel, circle'.
intro.cn: anticyclone 由 anti-「反向」加 cyclone 构成，后者源自希腊语 kyklos「轮、圆」。

items.en: The root *kwekwlos meant 'wheel', a reduplicated form still visible in cycle and wheel.
items.cn: 词根 *kwekwlos 意为「轮」，是叠音形式，仍见于 cycle 与 wheel。

items.en: Kyklos meant 'circle, wheel', giving cycle, bicycle, and encyclopedia.
items.cn: kyklos 意为「圆、轮」，生出 cycle、bicycle、encyclopedia。

items.en: Kyklon named a whirling storm, a wheel of wind.
items.cn: kyklon 指旋转的风暴，一座风之轮。

items.en: Once cyclone named the inward-spiraling storm, meteorologists coined anticyclone for its opposite twin.
items.cn: cyclone 定名内旋风暴后，气象学家为其孪生反面造出 anticyclone。

items.en: In the northern hemisphere anticyclone winds turn clockwise; in the southern, counterclockwise.
items.cn: 北半球反气旋风顺时针转；南半球逆时针转。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wheel family and anti- weather words; the near-meaning group gathers calm-weather terms.
note.cn: 形近组收「轮」词族与 anti- 气象词；近义组收晴稳天气用语。

entries.definition: The low-pressure twin: winds spiral inward, weather turns stormy.
entries.definitionCN: 低压孪生词：风向内旋，天气转 stormy。

entries.definition: An upward fold in rock layers; looks alike, but the root is geology, not wind.
entries.definitionCN: 背斜，岩层上拱；拼形相近，但属地质而非气象。

entries.definition: All-round education; shares kyklos 'circle' in a bookish way.
entries.definitionCN: 百科全书；以书面方式共享 kyklos「圆」。

entries.definition: A high-pressure area on the weather map, marked H.
entries.definitionCN: 天气图上标注 H 的高压区。

entries.definition: An elongated area of high pressure between two lows.
entries.definitionCN: 两个低压之间的高压脊。

entries.definition: Any system that brings calm, settled conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指带来晴稳天气的系统。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the anti- reversal, the cyclone wheel, and the weather-map picture.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 anti- 的反向、cyclone 的风轮，以及天气图画面。

normal.en: anti + cyclone: the wheel that turns the opposite way.
normal.cn: anti 加 cyclone：转向相反的风轮。

normal.en: Cyclone spins inward with storms; anticyclone outward with calm.
normal.cn: 气旋内旋带来风暴；反气旋外旋带来平静。

normal.en: On the map, find the letter H: that is the anticyclone.
normal.cn: 在天气图上找字母 H：那就是反气旋。

normal.en: Bicycle shares the wheel root: two wheels.
normal.cn: bicycle 共享「轮」词根：两个轮子。

normal.en: Anticyclonic is its adjective, as in anticyclonic gloom.
normal.cn: 形容词是 anticyclonic，如 anticyclonic gloom。

abstract.en: Picture a giant silent pinwheel turning outward over a quiet city.
abstract.cn: 想象一座巨大无声的风车在城市上空向外旋转。

abstract.en: Picture a week of flat gray fog under an unmoving sky.
abstract.cn: 想象停滞的天空下连日的灰色平雾。

abstract.en: Picture two spinning tops, one blowing outward, one sucking inward.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚旋转的陀螺，一个向外吹，一个向内吸。

examples.en: The anticyclone stalled, so the smog could not disperse.
examples.cn: 反气旋停滞，烟雾无法散去。

examples.en: Autumn anticyclones give crisp, cloudless days.
examples.cn: 秋季反气旋带来干爽无云的日子。

examples.en: Sailors read the anticyclone as a promise of light winds.
examples.cn: 水手把反气旋读作微风将至的许诺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安台赛克隆」——安稳的天气台风被赛着克隆成了平静版，就是「反气旋」

root: 希腊语 anti-（反向）+ kyklon（旋转的风暴，出自 kyklos「轮」）→ 反气旋；与气旋相反的高压外旋系统。

sensesIntro.en: One sense names the high-pressure system; the other reads the same anti- as a plain reversal of spin.
sensesIntro.cn: 第一义项命名高压系统；第二义项把同一个 anti- 读作转向的单纯反转。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slowly outward-turning wheel of air with clear skies pinned at its hub
core.cn: 核心意象：缓缓外旋的空气之轮，轮毂上钉着一片晴空

branches.en: The calm line: settled skies under a high.
branches.cn: 平静线：高压之下天空安稳。

branches.en: The haze line: the same stillness can trap smog.
branches.cn: 霾线：同样的静稳也会困住烟雾。

branches.en: The mirror line: anticyclone exists against its storm twin.
branches.cn: 镜像线：反气旋与风暴孪生词相对而立。

branches.en: The map line: the letter H names it in every forecast.
branches.cn: 地图线：每张天气图都用字母 H 标出它。

branches.en: Both senses share one reversed wheel, of weather or of water.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一个反转的风轮，或在天空，或在海洋。

intro.en: The compound shows anti- attached to cyclone, a Greek wheel-storm.
intro.cn: 这个复合词是把 anti- 加在希腊语的「风轮」cyclone 上。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family; the entries record the Greek source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁词族；条目记录希腊语源头。

items.example: It supplies the reversal in anticyclone.
items.exampleCN: 它为 anticyclone 提供反向义。

items.example: It appears in cycle, bicycle, cyclone.
It forms cyclone from kyklos.
items.exampleCN: 它由 kyklos 构成 cyclone。

items.example: It forms anticyclonic.
It forms anticyclones.

items.meaning: a whirling storm of low pressure
items.example: It is the stem the prefix attaches to.
It forms bicycle, two wheels.

items.meaning: a tropical cyclone in the Atlantic
items.example: It names the same wind wheel in a different ocean.
items.exampleCN: 它指另一片海洋的同一座风轮。

items.meaning: a tropical cyclone in the western Pacific
items.example: It is the Pacific name for the wheel of wind.
items.exampleCN: 它是风之轮在太平洋的名字。

definition_zh: 居住；住所；人类定居的痕迹；居住权
definition_en: the act of living in a place; a place where people live; the fact of an area having been lived in
core_image: 河湾边几间石屋围着一口水井，炊烟连成一条线，远处是无人走动的荒坡
scene: 测绘员在荒原边缘发现了几处废弃的石屋。 The surveyors found traces of former habitation at the edge of the moor.
sceneCN: 这里 habitation 指「人类居住留下的痕迹」（第 3 个义项：某地曾有人居住的证据）；句意为测绘员在荒原边缘发现了旧日居住的痕迹。图中可辨识物件：石墙残基、井口、塌落的屋顶、草甸。

pos.zh: 居住；住所；（某地的）居住痕迹
居住权（大陆法系中的一种物权）

derivatives.zh: 居住于；栖居于（前缀 in- 表示「在内」）
可居住的（-able 表示「能够」）
无人居住的（un- 加 -ed 构成否定形容词）

senses.title: The act of living in a place
senses.definition: the act or fact of living in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地点生活这一行为或事实
senses.example: Signs of habitation appeared only after the river changed course.
senses.exampleCN: 直到河流改道之后，才出现居住的迹象。
senses.why: habitation is the Latin noun of action from habitare 'to dwell', so its first job is to name the act, not the building.
senses.whyCN: habitation 是拉丁动词 habitare「居住」的行为名词，因此它首先指动作，而不是建筑。

senses.title: A place where someone lives
senses.definition: a place in which someone lives, especially a simple or isolated one
senses.definitionCN: 某人生活的地方，尤指简陋或偏僻的住所
senses.example: The trapper built a habitation of logs and turf beside the creek.
senses.exampleCN: 捕兽人在溪边用原木和草皮搭了一处住所。
senses.why: Latin already used the same noun for the result as well as the act, so English inherited both readings at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本就用同一个名词兼指动作与结果，英语因此同时继承了两层意思。

senses.title: Evidence that people lived in an area
senses.definition: the fact or signs of people having lived in an area, as shown by remains
senses.definitionCN: 某地曾有人居住的事实或迹象，以遗存为证
senses.example: Charred stones marked the first habitation on the plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 烧黑的石块标出了高原上最早的居住痕迹。
senses.why: field surveys needed a word for occupancy itself, so habitation came to mean the trace of living rather than the dwelling.
senses.whyCN: 野外调查需要一个指「占用」本身的词，habitation 于是指居住的痕迹，而非房屋。

senses.title: The condition of being fit to live in
senses.definition: the condition of being safe and suitable for people to live in
senses.definitionCN: 安全且适合人居住的状态
senses.example: Inspectors judged the block unfit for habitation.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员判定这栋楼不宜居住。
senses.why: housing law asks whether a place can be lived in at all, and the noun supplied that abstract condition.
senses.whyCN: 住房法规要判断一个地方究竟能否住人，这个名词正好提供了这一抽象状态。

senses.title: A dwelling counted as a housing unit
senses.titleCN: 作为住房单位计数的住所
senses.definition: a house or flat treated as one unit of housing in records
senses.definitionCN: 在登记中被视为一个住房单位的房屋或公寓
senses.example: The new rule applies to every habitation with its own kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定适用于每一套带独立厨房的住所。
senses.why: administration prefers a countable noun, and habitation was narrowed to one self-contained place of living.
senses.whyCN: 行政文书偏爱可数名词，habitation 因此被收窄为「一套独立住所」。

senses.title: A legal right to live in another's house
senses.definition: a limited right in civil law to live in a house owned by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 大陆法系中在他人家中居住的有限权利
senses.example: Her will granted him a habitation for the rest of his life.
senses.exampleCN: 她的遗嘱授予他终身居住权。
senses.why: Roman law separated the right to use a house from ownership, and the old noun was kept for that right.
senses.whyCN: 罗马法把房屋的使用权与所有权分开，这个古老名词就被保留下来指该项权利。

senses.title: A small settlement or group of homes
senses.definition: a group of homes forming a small settlement, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 由若干住宅构成的小型聚落，常用复数
senses.example: Scattered habitations dot the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 零散的居民点散布在谷底。
senses.why: plural use turns the word into a map label for a cluster of homes rather than one building.
senses.whyCN: 复数用法把这个词变成地图上标注一片住宅的标签，而非单座建筑。

senses.title: A place associated with a divine presence
senses.definition: a place associated with a god or an unseen being said to be present there
senses.definitionCN: 与神灵或无形存在有关的处所
senses.example: The grove was treated as the habitation of the forest spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 那片树林被视为林灵的居所。
senses.why: religious language extended the ordinary noun for living somewhere to beings that are not seen.
senses.whyCN: 宗教语言把日常表示「住在某处」的名词，扩展到看不见的存在身上。

intro.en: Habitation comes from Latin habitatio 'a dwelling', from habitare 'to dwell', which is a frequentative form of habere 'to have, hold'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: habitation 来自拉丁 habitatio「住所」，源自 habitare「居住」，而 habitare 是 habere「持有」的反复动词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habere meant 'to have, hold, keep'. The often-cited Indo-European base is a reconstruction, and how 'hold' turned into 'dwell' is debated.
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、持有、守住」。常被引用的印欧语词基属于重构形式，而「持有」如何转为「居住」仍有争论。

items.en: Habitare, a frequentative of habere, meant 'to dwell, to keep on occupying a place', literally 'to be holding' it.
items.cn: habitare 是 habere 的反复形式，意为「居住、持续占有一地」，字面就是「一直持有着」。

items.en: The action noun habitatio named both the act of dwelling and the place where one dwells.
items.cn: 行为名词 habitatio 同时指「居住」这一动作和「居住的地方」。

items.en: Old French habitation brought the word into English in the thirteenth century, first as the act and soon after as the place.
items.cn: 古法语 habitation 在十三世纪把该词带入英语，先指动作，很快也指地点。

items.en: Civil-law texts kept a specialised sense, the right of habitation, meaning a limited personal right to live in another's house.
items.cn: 大陆法文本保留了一个专门义「居住权」，指在他人家中居住的有限人身权利。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not fixed to a single year, and the pre-Latin base of habere is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语书证无法系于某一年，habere 的拉丁语前词基属于重构形式而非有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical forms that come from the same Latin verb but mean different things; group two holds nouns that also speak of living somewhere.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，同出拉丁动词却意义不同；第二组是同样表示「住在某处」的名词。

entries.definition: The natural environment in which a species lives, not the building or settlement; it is the sense ecology fixed for the word.
entries.definitionCN: 指物种生活的自然环境，而非建筑或聚落；这是生态学为它固定的含义。

entries.definition: From Latin habitus 'condition, bearing', it means a repeated behaviour or a garment worn by monks, not a place of living.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 habitus「状态、举止」，指重复的习惯或僧侣的袍服，并非居住之处。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus habitare: the verb meaning to live in a place, from which inhabitant is formed.
entries.definitionCN: in-「在内」加 habitare：表示居住在某地的动词，inhabitant 由它构成。

entries.definition: Built on habit in its behaviour sense, meaning done regularly; it belongs to the habit branch, not the dwelling branch.
entries.definitionCN: 由「习惯」义的 habit 构成，意为惯常的；属于「习惯」分支，而非「居住」分支。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the house or shelter where someone lives; habitation is more formal and can mean the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指人所住房屋或遮蔽处的日常名词；habitation 更正式，且可指居住行为。

entries.definition: A formal word for a home, often an imposing house or an official one; it stresses status more than shelter.
entries.definitionCN: 指住所的正式用词，常指气派的宅第或官邸，更强调身份而非遮蔽。

entries.definition: The fact of using or living in a space, often temporary or legally measured; it does not imply a permanent home.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用或占用一处空间的事实，常为临时或按法规计量；并不暗示永久安家。

entries.definition: A place where people have settled as a community, larger than a single dwelling and mapped as a group.
entries.definitionCN: 人们作为群体定居的地方，规模大于单座住所，在地图上成片标出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: habere 'hold' plus the frequentative -itare: to keep holding a place, hence to dwell there.
normal.cn: habere「持有」加反复后缀 -itare：一直持有一地，因此就是住在那里。

normal.en: The same root gives inhabit, inhabitant, habitable and uninhabited.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 inhabit、inhabitant、habitable 与 uninhabited。

normal.en: Legal phrases keep the old noun alive: right of habitation, fit for habitation.
normal.cn: 法律短语让这个古老名词延续：居住权、适宜居住。

normal.en: Keep habitat apart: habitat is the environment, habitation is the living there.
normal.cn: 要把 habitat 分清：habitat 是环境，habitation 是居住这件事。

normal.en: Surveys say signs of habitation when they mean traces of people, not houses still standing.
normal.cn: 调查报告说「居住痕迹」时，指的是人留下的痕迹，而非仍然立着的房屋。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint that outlasts the foot, which is exactly what a trace of habitation is.
abstract.cn: 想象一个比脚留得更久的脚印，居住痕迹正是如此。

abstract.en: Picture a key that grants the right to sleep under a roof without owning it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，给人睡在屋顶下的权利，却不给所有权。

abstract.en: Picture a map with three dots that mean homes rather than points.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上三个圆点，它们代表的是家，而不是坐标。

examples.en: The valley has shown continuous habitation for more than four thousand years.
examples.cn: 这个山谷显示出四千多年连续不断的居住史。

examples.en: The council declared the building unfit for habitation after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，市政会宣布该建筑不宜居住。

examples.en: A few habitations cling to the slope above the road.
examples.cn: 几处住所紧贴在大路以上的山坡上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「habit（习惯）+ ation」——习惯待在一个地方 → 居住、住所

root: 拉丁 habere「持有」→ 反复动词 habitare「一直占有一地、居住」→ 名词 habitatio「居住；住所」。habere 的拉丁语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one Latin act noun: holding a place becomes living there, then the place itself, the trace left behind, the legal right to stay, and even a god's home.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由一个拉丁行为名词展开：持有一地成为居住，继而指处所本身、留下的痕迹、居住的权利，甚至神灵的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that keeps hold of one spot of ground until staying there becomes living there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手始终抓住一小块地面，抓久了，停留就成了居住。

branches.en: ACT AND PLACE: the same Latin noun named both the living there and the place where it happens.
branches.cn: 动作与地点：同一个拉丁名词既指居住，也指居住之处。

branches.en: TRACE: surveyors read the remains of living as evidence that the place was once inhabited.
branches.cn: 痕迹：调查者把生活遗存读作「这里曾有人住」的证据。

branches.en: MEASURED LIVING: law asks whether a place is fit to live in and counts it as one housing unit.
branches.cn: 可量度的居住：法律判断一处能否住人，并把它计作一个住房单位。

branches.en: RIGHT: Roman law split use from ownership, leaving a limited personal right to live in another's house.
branches.cn: 权利：罗马法把使用与所有权分开，留下在他人家中居住的有限人身权利。

branches.en: MAP AND MYTH: the plural labels a cluster of homes, and religious language lends the noun to unseen beings.
branches.cn: 地图与神话：复数形式标注一片住宅，宗教语言则把这个名词借给看不见的存在。

intro.en: Habitation is built entirely from Latin material: a root meaning 'hold', a frequentative suffix and a noun suffix, all still productive in English.
intro.cn: habitation 完全由拉丁材料构成：意为「持有」的词根、反复后缀与名词后缀，这些成分在英语中仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere gives habitation, inhabit, inhabitant, habitable, habit and habitat; in- adds 'within', while -atio forms the action noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habere 衍生 habitation、inhabit、inhabitant、habitable、habit 与 habitat；in- 增添「在内」，-atio 构成行为名词。

items.example: The root carries the idea of holding on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「抓住不放」的意思。

items.meaning: to do something repeatedly or intensively
items.example: The suffix makes holding into continuing to hold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「持有」变成「持续持有」。

items.meaning: to dwell, to keep occupying a place
items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语名词的直接来源。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成动作的名称。

items.meaning: living in a place; a place lived in
items.example: The word covers both the act and the place.
items.exampleCN: 这个词兼指动作与地点。

items.example: Few animals inhabit the salt flat.
items.exampleCN: 很少有动物栖居在这片盐滩。

items.meaning: one who lives in a place
items.example: The island has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛的居民不到一百人。

items.example: Only the lower slopes are habitable.
items.exampleCN: 只有较低的山坡可以住人。

items.meaning: the environment where a species lives
items.example: Drainage destroyed the bird's habitat.
items.exampleCN: 排水工程毁掉了这种鸟的栖息地。

latinEntries.meaning: a dwelling; the act of dwelling

definition_zh: 地形的；地形学的；与地表起伏测绘有关的
definition_en: relating to the shape, elevation, and detailed description of a land surface
core_image: 一张布满等高线的图纸，密集线条标出陡坡
scene: 工程队摊开一张带等高线的图纸，沿着密集的线条判断坡度： Engineers read a topographic map before routing the new road.
sceneCN: 这里 topographic 指「与地表起伏测绘有关的」（第 2 个义项：以等高线等表示地形的地图）；句意为工程师在规划新路前阅读地形图。

pos.zh: 地形的；地形学的；地形测绘的

senses.title: Relating to surface shape
senses.definition: concerning the form, slope, and arrangement of features on a land surface
senses.definitionCN: 关于陆地表面的形态、坡度与要素排列
senses.example: Topographic relief controls where water gathers.
senses.exampleCN: 地形起伏决定水在哪里汇集。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the idea of place-description to any noun, so a feature becomes topographic when its shape matters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「描述地方」的观念附着到任何名词上，因此当形状重要时，某要素就是地形的。

senses.title: Of a map with contours
senses.titleCN: 以等高线表示地形的地图
senses.definition: describing a map that shows elevation and surface form, usually with contour lines
senses.definitionCN: 描述以等高线等符号显示高程与地表形态的地图
senses.example: Engineers read a topographic map before routing the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在规划新路前阅读地形图。
senses.why: A topographic map is the standard product of the discipline, so the adjective became part of the map's name.
senses.whyCN: 地形图是该学科的标准产品，因此这个形容词成了地图名称的一部分。

senses.title: Of a survey or measurement
senses.definition: relating to the measurement of elevations and positions on the ground
senses.definitionCN: 与地面高程与位置的测量有关
senses.example: The topographic survey fixed the height of every corner.
senses.exampleCN: 地形测量确定了每个角点的高程。
senses.why: Surveying turns terrain into numbers, and the adjective marks that measured kind of work.
senses.whyCN: 测量把地形变成数字，这个形容词标记的正是这种测量工作。

senses.title: Of differences in elevation
senses.definition: describing variation in height across an area that affects climate, drainage, or travel
senses.definitionCN: 描述一个地区内影响气候、排水或通行的高度变化
senses.example: Topographic barriers keep the wet air on the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 地形屏障把湿空气挡在海岸。
senses.why: Height difference is the most measurable part of surface shape, so it often takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 高差是地表形状中最可测量的部分，因此常由这个形容词修饰。

senses.title: Of named surface features
senses.definition: relating to specific features such as ridges, valleys, and scarps shown on a survey
senses.definitionCN: 与测量图上显示的山脊、谷地、陡坎等具体要素有关
senses.example: Each topographic feature was labelled with its elevation.
senses.exampleCN: 每个地形要素都标注了高程。
senses.why: Once features are catalogued, the adjective distinguishes them from cultural or biological features.
senses.whyCN: 要素被编目后，这个形容词把它们与文化或生物要素区分开。

senses.title: Of military ground advantage
senses.definition: describing ground features that give a tactical advantage, such as height or cover
senses.definitionCN: 描述提供战术优势（如高度或掩蔽）的地面特征
senses.example: Topographic control decided the outcome of the skirmish.
senses.exampleCN: 地形控制权决定了这场小规模交战的结果。
senses.why: Armies read ground as advantage, so topographic becomes a staff word for position and visibility.
senses.whyCN: 军队把地面读作优势，因此 topographic 成为参谋用语，指位置与通视。

senses.title: Of medical surface profiling
senses.definition: relating to the mapped curvature of a body surface, especially the cornea
senses.definitionCN: 与体表（尤其角膜）曲率的测绘有关
senses.example: Topographic imaging showed the cornea's uneven curve.
senses.exampleCN: 地形成像显示了角膜不平整的曲率。
senses.why: The adjective is generic enough to describe any surface whose highs and lows must be mapped.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词足够通用，可描述任何必须测绘高低起伏的表面。

senses.title: Abstract: structurally arranged
senses.definition: describing the overall structural layout of an idea, field, or system
senses.definitionCN: 描述某一观念、领域或系统的整体结构布局
senses.example: The essay offers a topographic view of the novel's themes.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章提供了小说主题的地形式视角。
senses.why: The metaphor treats abstract elements as features on a surface, with peaks, basins, and connections.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把抽象要素当作地表上的特征，有峰、有盆、有连接。

intro.en: Topographic is the Greek-derived adjective of topography, formed with -ikos. The elements are recorded; the origin of topos is not. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: topographic 是 topography 的希腊语来源形容词，由 -ikos 构成。语素有书证，topos 的来源不明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Topos meant 'place'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the Indo-European links sometimes proposed are reconstructions, not proved derivations.
items.cn: topos 意为「地方」。其更深来源不确定；有时提出的印欧语关联是重构形式，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Topographikos meant 'of place-description', built on topographia with the adjective suffix -ikos.
items.cn: topographikos 意为「属于地方描述的」，由 topographia 加形容词后缀 -ikos 构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as topographicus, and English shortened it to topographic.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊形容词作 topographicus，英语再缩短为 topographic。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the adjective attached to maps and surveys that showed elevation.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，这个形容词附着于显示高程的地图与测量。

items.en: Medical and microscopic uses are modern; their exact first dates are not fixed.
items.cn: 医学与微观用途属现代用法，其确切首见年代未固定。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Greek stock that are easily swapped; group two holds adjectives for related kinds of shape and mapping.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊语词干、极易互换的形式；第二组是描述相关形状与制图的形容词。

entries.definition: The longer adjective with the same meaning; British usage often prefers it in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 意义相同的较长形容词；英式正式写作常用它。

entries.definition: The subject or the surface arrangement itself; topographic is the adjective that modifies other nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 学科或地表排列本身；topographic 是修饰其它名词的形容词。

entries.definition: The person who measures surfaces; it cannot modify a noun such as map.
entries.definitionCN: 测量地表的人；它不能修饰 map 之类的名词。

entries.definition: Relating to printing and type design, from typos 'impression'; it has nothing to do with land.
entries.definitionCN: 与印刷和字体设计有关，来自 typos「印记」；与土地无关。

entries.definition: Relating to geography as a whole, including human and regional patterns; topographic concerns surface shape.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地理学有关，包括人文与区域格局；topographic 关注地表形状。

entries.definition: Relating to the design and production of maps rather than to the land's shape itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与地图设计与制作有关，而非土地形状本身。

entries.definition: Relating to the measurement and statistical description of elevation; a narrower technical term.
entries.definitionCN: 与高程测量及统计描述有关；范围更窄的技术术语。

entries.definition: Relating to the origin and development of landforms rather than to their mapped shape.
entries.definitionCN: 与地貌的成因与发育有关，而非其测绘形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek morphemes, real mapping terms and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实希腊语素、真实制图术语与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Topographic map is the fixed phrase; the adjective rarely appears alone in everyday speech.
normal.cn: topographic map 是固定短语；这个形容词在日常中很少单独出现。

normal.en: Topography is the noun; topographer is the person; topographic is the adjective.
normal.cn: topography 是名词，topographer 是人，topographic 是形容词。

normal.en: Contours are the signature of a topographic sheet.
normal.cn: 等高线是地形图的标志。

normal.en: Do not confuse topographic with typographic: land versus type.
normal.cn: 不要把 topographic 与 typographic 混淆：一个是土地，一个是字体。

normal.en: Topographic relief means the range of heights, not emotional relief.
normal.cn: topographic relief 指高度差，不是情绪上的宽慰。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper that tells you where the ground rises before you arrive.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸，在你到达之前就告诉你地面哪里升高。

abstract.en: Picture a surface described entirely by lines that never cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一个表面完全由永不相交的线条描述。

abstract.en: Picture an argument drawn as a map of peaks and basins.
abstract.cn: 想象一场论证被画成有峰有盆的地图。

examples.en: Engineers read a topographic map before routing the new road.
examples.cn: 工程师在规划新路前阅读地形图。

examples.en: The topographic survey recorded a steep scarp behind the town.
examples.cn: 地形测量记录了镇后的陡坎。

examples.en: Topographic relief explains why the two valleys have different rainfall.
examples.cn: 地形起伏解释了为什么两条谷地降水不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「topo（地方）+ graphic（描绘的）」——描绘一个地方高低起伏的 → 地形的

root: 拉丁语 topographicus，来自希腊语 topographikos = topos「地方」+ graphein「书写」+ -ikos「……的」。topos 更深来源不确定，所提印欧关联均属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from surface shape to contour maps, surveys, elevation differences, named features, military ground, medical profiling, and finally abstract structure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从地表形状走到等高线图、测量、高程差、命名要素、军事地形、医学测绘，最后落到抽象结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet full of contour lines, packed tightly where the slope is steep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张布满等高线的图纸，坡陡处线条密集。

branches.en: SHAPE AND MEASUREMENT: the adjective covers both what the surface is and how it is measured.
branches.cn: 形状与测量：这个形容词既指表面是什么样，也指如何测量它。

branches.en: MAP AND FEATURES: contours turn a surface into a sheet, and named features give it a vocabulary.
branches.cn: 地图与要素：等高线把表面变成图纸，命名要素则给它一套词汇。

branches.en: HEIGHT AS POWER: the same elevation that controls drainage also controls visibility and defence.
branches.cn: 高度即力量：控制排水的高程，也控制通视与防御。

branches.en: SCALE SHIFT: the cornea is mapped with the same logic as a mountain range.
branches.cn: 尺度转换：角膜与山脉用同一逻辑测绘。

branches.en: METAPHOR: abstract ideas acquire peaks, basins, and connecting routes.
branches.cn: 比喻：抽象观念获得山峰、盆地与连接路径。

intro.en: The adjective is built from the topography stem plus the Greek adjective ending -ic.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由 topography 词干加希腊形容词词尾 -ic 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin topographicus and Greek topographikos stand behind the word; topos and graphein are the ultimate elements.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 topographicus 与希腊语 topographikos 支撑这个词；topos 与 graphein 是最终语素。

items.example: Topos supplies the place element.
-Graphic appears in geographic and topographic.
Topography is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: topography 是这个形容词背后的名词。

items.meaningCN: 地形的；与地表形状有关的
items.example: A topographic map shows elevation.
Topographical writing describes the ground in detail.
items.exampleCN: 地形描述文字详细描写地面。

items.example: The pass is topographically the lowest route.
items.exampleCN: 这个山口在地形上是最低的路线。

items.example: The topographer worked from the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 地形测绘者从山脊上作业。

items.example: Bathymetric data mirror topographic data underwater.
items.exampleCN: 测深数据是地形数据在水下的对应物。

items.example: A hypsometric curve summarizes topographic relief.
items.exampleCN: 高程曲线概括了地形起伏。

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin topographicus, from Greek topographikos

definition_zh: 演示的；示范的；（语法）指示的；感情外露的
definition_en: showing or explaining something by visible example; (grammar) pointing out a particular person or thing; openly displaying feelings
core_image: 一只手把物件举到众人眼前，让所有人都看清它的样子
scene: 这里指「演示的」。 The demonstrative model on the bench let every student see how the pump worked.
sceneCN: 这里 demonstrative 是「演示用的、示范的」（第 1 个义项：把结构摆出来给人看）；句意：长凳上那个演示模型让每个学生都看清了泵如何工作。图中可辨识物件：长凳、透明泵体模型、围坐的学生、指向模型的手。

pos.zh: 演示的；示范的；指示的；感情外露的

senses.title: Shown by visible example
senses.definition: serving to show how something works by displaying it rather than only describing it
senses.definitionCN: 以展示实物或动作、而非只靠描述来说明某物如何运作的
senses.example: The demonstrative model of the engine let visitors see every moving part.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机的演示模型让参观者看到了每一个运动部件。
senses.why: monstrare means 'to show'. The de- prefix intensifies the showing, so a demonstrative thing does not merely mention a process, it puts the process in front of the eyes.
senses.whyCN: monstrare 意为“显示”。de- 前缀加强了这个“显示”，因此 demonstrative 的东西不只是提到某个过程，而是把过程摆到眼睛前面。

senses.title: Teaching by demonstration
senses.definition: using a practical display as the method of teaching or explaining
senses.definitionCN: 以实际操作展示作为教学或解释方法的
senses.example: Her demonstrative style of teaching kept the class awake.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种示范式的教学风格让全班都保持清醒。
senses.why: A demonstration places the action beside the explanation. The suffix -ive marks the quality of showing, so the adjective names a method whose tool is visible action.
senses.whyCN: 示范把动作放在讲解旁边。-ive 标记“显示”的性质，因此这个形容词命名的是一种以可见动作为工具的方法。

senses.title: Grammar: pointing outward
senses.titleCN: 指示的：手指向某一个人或物
senses.definition: in grammar, marking a specific person or thing, as this, that, these and those do
senses.definitionCN: 语法上标记特定的人或物，如 this、that、these、those 所做的那样
senses.example: In 'this book', the word 'this' is a demonstrative adjective.
senses.exampleCN: 在 this book 中，this 是指示形容词。
senses.why: The grammatical sense keeps the literal gesture: a demonstrative word points. deictic pointing and the physical pointing hand share the same monstrare image of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 语法义保留了字面手势：指示词就是用手一指。语法上的指认与用手指出，共享同一个 monstrare“把注意力引过去”的意象。

senses.title: Openly affectionate
senses.titleCN: 感情外露的：抱一下就看得见
senses.definition: showing love or affection openly through hugs, kisses or warm words
senses.definitionCN: 通过拥抱、亲吻或亲热言语公开表达爱意或亲情的
senses.example: He is a demonstrative father who hugs his children every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个感情外露的父亲，每天早上都要抱抱孩子。
senses.why: The 19th-century extension moves from showing objects to showing feelings. The feeling is treated as something held out in the hand, where others can see it.
